name: David Hogg
subject: This is why I left the DNC
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY LEADERS WE DESERVE, LEADERSWEDESERVE
body:
We deserve better Democrats.
# [](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/852?refcode=em20260121-1&t=1&akid=3071%2E587540%2Eqk0g0G)
**Peter, this is exactly why I left the DNC:**
Even after Democrats faced historic losses in 2024, and allowed Trump back into the White House, a lot of folks in the establishment are _STILL_ convinced that we need to play it safe. They don’t want us to challenge sitting Democrats in safe seats.
I’m no longer a DNC Vice Chair because I decided that I could make more of an impact electing the next generation of leaders here at Leaders We Deserve.
Too many Democrats in D.C. are silent, complacent, and beholden to special interests. They treat public office like something they’re owed — not a responsibility to earn from the people they serve. To get our party out of this moment we have no other choice but to embrace rigorous competition in our safe blue seats to challenge ourselves to be better. We need voters to turn out for us because they actually believe in our vision for the future of the country not simply because we’re not Republicans.
At Leaders We Deserve, we’re building a new generation of young, progressive leaders — an inspiring vision for the Democratic Party that people actually like and are excited to vote for. Importantly, these young leaders are not just younger versions of the people currently in power. They are principled leaders with the backing from us so they can remain independent of special interest groups. That's why we exist — not just to elect young people but to give people of all ages a genuine sense of hope that while politics is broken there is a new generation of young leaders coming into power who aren’t corrupt and will actually represent them. To do that we have to elect better leaders in our purple seats and our blue seats and challenge those in our own party who fail to meet the moment.
That is exactly why we’re endorsing Democratic primary challengers like Justin J. Pearson and Donavan McKinney — and we’re doing it because Democrats deserve better than ineffective leaders who cling to power instead of working for their constituents.
**We can flip the script and send new leaders to Washington — young progressives who are ready to fight for what matters.**
**[We refuse corporate money, as do our candidates. Making this change is hard but we can do it with your support. Will you pitch in $5 now?](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260121_1_dnc._2zBGP&refcode=em20260121-3071&amount=5&t=2&akid=3071%2E587540%2Eqk0g0G)**

Thank you,
David

clean_body: We deserve better Democrats. Peter, this is exactly why I left the DNC: Even after Democrats faced historic losses in 2024, and allowed Trump back into the White House, a lot of folks in the establishment are STILL convinced that we need to play it safe. They don’t want us to challenge sitting Democrats in safe seats. I’m no longer a DNC Vice Chair because I decided that I could make more of an impact electing the next generation of leaders here at Leaders We Deserve. Too many Democrats in D.C. are silent, complacent, and beholden to special interests. They treat public office like something they’re owed — not a responsibility to earn from the people they serve. To get our party out of this moment we have no other choice but to embrace rigorous competition in our safe blue seats to challenge ourselves to be better. We need voters to turn out for us because they actually believe in our vision for the future of the country not simply because we’re not Republicans. At Leaders We Deserve, we’re building a new generation of young, progressive leaders — an inspiring vision for the Democratic Party that people actually like and are excited to vote for. Importantly, these young leaders are not just younger versions of the people currently in power. They are principled leaders with the backing from us so they can remain independent of special interest groups. That's why we exist — not just to elect young people but to give people of all ages a genuine sense of hope that while politics is broken there is a new generation of young leaders coming into power who aren’t corrupt and will actually represent them. To do that we have to elect better leaders in our purple seats and our blue seats and challenge those in our own party who fail to meet the moment. That is exactly why we’re endorsing Democratic primary challengers like Justin J. Pearson and Donavan McKinney — and we’re doing it because Democrats deserve better than ineffective leaders who cling to power instead of working for their constituents. We can flip the script and send new leaders to Washington — young progressives who are ready to fight for what matters. Thank you, David

body:
As a former CIA officer, I've seen democracies flicker out.
Folks, Several weeks ago, myself and five other Members of Congress with service and veteran backgrounds made a video directly quoting the Uniform Code of Military Justice about the military’s responsibility to reject illegal orders.

In response, President Trump called for my arrest, trial and death by hanging.

**Just recently, I learned that former Fox News host Jeanine Pirro, U.S. Attorney for the District of Columbia, asked to interview me.**

This is on top of the FBI’s Counterterrorism Division’s inquiry at the end of last year.

As a former CIA officer, I’ve seen democracies flicker out. I’ve seen what life is like when a government is rigged. I’ve studied this kind of political authoritarianism in other countries where you can’t criticize the guys in charge without getting a knock at the door in the middle of the night.

It’s hard to believe I am talking about it in my own country, and the knock is happening on my door.

I’ve always tried to be straight with you in these emails. When these threats happen, it requires a strategy — because no American wants to live in a country where the president can weaponize the government against his perceived enemies.

We don't have to sit around waiting for these Supreme Court decisions. All the recent election results show that, when we have the time and resources to organize, we can elect pro-voter candidates who will enact pro-democracy policies and protect our right to vote.
We need to organize, register voters, inform them about the election, and get them to cast their ballot in whatever way they can. RUSH $35 or more and help us make every vote count this November, in 2028, and beyond >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=012126_3&amount=35]
Voter Action Project [https://voteractionproject.org/]
Axios - Scoop: GOP expects SCOTUS boost [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=012126_3&amount=25]
Straight from Axios , Team: " President Trump's political team privately told big donors that the Supreme Court will soon issue rulings on voting rights and contribution limits that could tilt future elections their way. "
Two main cases are making the MAGA movement feel like things are going to break their way ahead of the 2026 elections:
➜ In Louisiana v. Callais , the court is set to decide whether to gut Section 2 of the Voting Rights Act (VRA) and return to a time of racial gerrymandering. This would be the capstone of Chief Justice John Roberts career, as he's been working to neuter the VRA since he worked for Ronald Reagan.
➜ In National Republican Senatorial Committee (NRSC) v. the Federal Elections Commission (FEC) , the court is tackling a case that could eliminate a federal law capping how much big-money party committees can spend in direct coordination with favored candidates. This could be the most consequential campaign finance case since the Citizens United decision opened the floodgates of corporate spending in our elections.
To be clear, these cases boil down to a simple idea: do voters get to make the decisions, or can politicians choose their voters and pump unlimited cash into their campaign coffers?

The potential consequences of these cases are simple to understand and grave for voter participation. The harder we make it to vote, the more politicians make voter participation feel worthless, the less people actually take part. Needless to say, the less people who participate, the less our democracy and our government looks like the people it's supposed to represent.
Section 2 of the VRA requires that racial minorities have an equal opportunity to meaningfully participate in the electoral process. Gutting Section 2 would take us backwards in time and allow racial gerrymandering to be a standard practice, silencing more voters.
In the NRSC case, there are limits on how much political parties and outside entities can coordinate financially with certain candidates. Removing these FEC limits would make it easier for the uber-rich to direct spending and influence elections , limiting the value of voters and making it harder for challengers to enter the political process.
Just like the redistricting fights across the country, this is all about whether the party in power can choose their voters in order to stay in power in perpetuity.

I served our country for 35 years, and I’m not done yet.
_[unsubscribe](https://secure.ngpvan.com/p/uV0Vq92dx0WQWrAIt9AKkw2?unsubscribedata=%2FZlJsNGfmwC%2Fr8z4qxGnIu3fK6dlTRO%2BmPN7I3bPz7iUOTjyrtAM8WlQQ9BIZ9ojQ1KWk3f2CpvxutEpQydb4%2FuqLfqyvSy9Pf8cZmEywQqmw4wJdvdQH%2Bz1kY2U1CwxcZ8NnYxOzjYxrRuTZQCPk8MfmOhpXg6sHowTs8x%2FwkSHuXollKtWztgvpd34LTtZumckaXfOsbkog8ll8UcTWhP47jlZcfTzOMxkitfcqPtfCth3Tk1eJaKGUqm%2BW7xTQKNdHtX0ESa4rbloHWKMJXVD6ssV0khPQyS%2F2QJv3as%2F1UsCPPDkH16ZA%2BQvl%2FArWTHx%2FKzMxYxY2ob7JiWr3BNvR%2B2Ibi6dz4S6ikcBF%2FSqEKOmfe%2FDPEfyYeHs9W2%2BP3fUUpTORG7uMWZn%2FvctsAAy%2F7aqBZppA%2BwTerjneM1hLXxgGwy4TNxnANx3KWU4)_

Hi,
After serving our country for 35 years in the Navy, I was removed from my position by Pete Hegseth without reason.
I spent my entire life in service to this country, always putting the mission and the people above myself. But when I was forced out, I had a choice: go out quietly, or _find a way to keep serving._
I’ve always lived by three simple ideals: honor, integrity, and respect. **That’s why I’m running for Congress in South Carolina’s first district.** [**If you believe that’s what we need in Washington right now, please consider splitting a donation between my campaign and Eileen Laubacher's.**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/123778487/596573782/-1420152198?refcode=20260121pm-nd&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjIvMS8xMTgxNzIiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiMGI5ZjNiZDEtMmZmNy1mMDExLThkNGMtMDAyMjQ4MmQyNzliIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=AtOhCPfB0mH3VfzcNNziRdSz-5dvezl6oDRj0Mj4Ykc=)
The day I was removed from my position, I was forced to leave behind my life’s work. I never went back to the Pentagon or wore the uniform again.
But this story isn’t just about me. Throughout the first year of Donald Trump’s second term, every woman serving as a three or four-star admiral in the Navy has been fired, forced out, or reassigned. This wasn’t an isolated incident. It’s a pattern.
When leadership decisions are driven by politics instead of integrity, our families, communities, and nation pay the price.
**That’s why I’m running for Congress:** to keep serving, to stand up when it’s hardest, and to fight for leadership that puts country over politics every time.
[**Early support in races like this matters most. We have a long road ahead of us if we’re going to fill this open seat and make the government work for the people again. If you can, please split a donation between my campaign and Eileen Laubacher's to help me hit the ground running and prove that service to our country shouldn’t end just because someone in power says it should.**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/123778488/596573783/-1420152198?refcode=20260121pm-nd&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjIvMS8xMTgxNzIiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiMGI5ZjNiZDEtMmZmNy1mMDExLThkNGMtMDAyMjQ4MmQyNzliIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=AtOhCPfB0mH3VfzcNNziRdSz-5dvezl6oDRj0Mj4Ykc=)
With my deepest respect and gratitude,
Nancy Lacore
_Democratic Candidate for Congress
South Carolina’s First District_

clean_body: We have a small window of opportunity to make our voices heard. | | | Peter, For months, we’ve seen ICE agents kidnap, beat, terrorize, and kill our community members. We’ve witnessed it with our own eyes. Millions have banded together to reject ICE and resist their escalations. And yet, as early as tomorrow, Congress is preparing to vote on a bill that would increase funding for this rogue agency. It’s abhorrent. And we have an extraordinarily small window of opportunity to make our voices heard. We can’t stop there, however. This Friday, January 23rd, Minnesotans are coming together for a statewide day of action: no work, no school, no shopping. Too many politicians don't even view ICE’s violence as a problem — they’re cheering it on. And many prominent Democrats think that this is an issue that can be fixed by simply expanding training requirements or handing out more body cameras. But body cameras would not have saved the life of Renee Good, who was executed in broad daylight, surrounded by cell phones, cameras, and recording devices. They would not have saved the life of Geraldo Lunas Campos, who was choked to death by guards at a detention facility in Texas on January 3rd.1 They would not have prevented ICE thugs from hospitalizing children with flashbang grenades and tear gas.2 And more training wouldn’t stop a rogue government agency like ICE, who have already been told they’re operating above the law. Writing them a bigger check is only going to increase the frequency and intensity of their violence against our communities. Thank you for being with us in this fight, Peter. In solidarity, Team WFP 1\. , The Washington Post, January 15, 2026 2\. , Fox 9 Minneapolis-St. Paul, January 15, 2026 Thoughts? Feedback? We want to hear it. # [Will Senate Democrats Vote to Fund Trump's Gestapo?](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=4981170&post_id=185318132&utm_source=post-email-title&utm_campaign=email-post-title&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MTg1MzE4MTMyLCJpYXQiOjE3NjkwNDY0MDAsImV4cCI6MTc3MTYzODQwMCwiaXNzIjoicHViLTQ5ODExNzAiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.NEQpMQrM4qRb7oYaXdkdKllv_cG8c2G0PkH5QshfBgs)
### The Democratic establishment is not rising to the occasion--but regular people, in Minneapolis and across the country, absolutely are.
| | [Aaron Regunberg](https://substack.com/@aaronregunberg)
---
| Jan 22
---
| [](https://substack.com/@aaronregunberg)
---

---

The contrast this week between ICE's outrageous conduct and the Democratic establishment's response to these abuses has been hard to reconcile.
On the one hand, we continue to see--in headlines, in videos, on our timelines, everywhere we look--ICE operating rabidly outside the bounds of what can be allowed to exist in a democratic society. ICE officers are [kidnapping](https://substack.com/redirect/a7940c8b-cd0a-4b38-86e9-95fb742c7d66?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) half-naked grandpas in the freezing cold; they're [denying](https://substack.com/redirect/3857dc26-3925-4f4b-913b-10a407ae71b3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) legal counsel to detainees; they're [entering](https://substack.com/redirect/2af36eca-5a1f-4e47-9ef2-52873f42ecc6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) homes without warrants; they're using chemical weapons [against](https://substack.com/redirect/06b80b01-d3e8-4b23-9657-4f40a3e2693f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) high school students; they're [sending](https://substack.com/redirect/27579a88-3f62-4595-930f-b36fc4b17e06?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) babies to the hospital. They are violently occupying American cities, acting--and in some cases [quite explicitly](https://substack.com/redirect/ad263315-2764-43d4-8746-e57fe3f43104?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) cosplaying--like the Gestapo that Trump wants them to be.
At the same time, as we speed towards one of Congressional Democrats' last remaining points of leverage against this regime--the January 30th [deadline](https://substack.com/redirect/7d86fa88-5b3d-4cda-bbc4-71fab45541ce?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to pass an appropriations bill to keep the government open--we're reading headlines like "[Congress clinches $1.2T funding deal for DHS...](https://substack.com/redirect/f03cbb20-f596-4f80-979e-6cb06f7eb903?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)" and "[Democrats support bill that would give ICE $10 billion](https://substack.com/redirect/bbaaf478-5d41-4bb4-a080-e71e96436de7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)." We're even seeing Democratic leaders [propose](https://substack.com/redirect/6d00db5d-adea-48f7-92b9-3979be2bf466?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) _more_ funding for ICE training and body cameras, just weeks after Jonathan Ross, a longtime ICE firearms instructor, _literally filmed himself_ shooting Renee Good in the face.
[Subscribed](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9hYXJvbnJlZ3VuYmVyZy5zdWJzdGFjay5jb20vYWNjb3VudCIsInAiOjE4NTMxODEzMiwicyI6NDk4MTE3MCwiZiI6dHJ1ZSwidSI6OTA1MDExOTIsImlhdCI6MTc2OTA0NjQwMCwiZXhwIjoyMDg0NjIyNDAwLCJpc3MiOiJwdWItMCIsInN1YiI6ImxpbmstcmVkaXJlY3QifQ.6Hi-oAViD6rHQHo5UomESMw2B_2pWOuLMOD08IYmUOY?)
**This is simply untenable. No rational, functioning opposition party would actively step in to fund the primary enforcement mechanism of the authoritarian takeover they ostensibly oppose.**
Voting to fund ICE in this moment is not only morally catastrophic--it is also politically absurd. Americans are seeing what ICE is doing, and they _don 't like it_. [Polling](https://substack.com/redirect/ccaf8915-8983-46a6-9b4f-793db04d5f3b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) shows that a majority of Americans view ICE unfavorably and support restrictions on the agency. And for nearly half of the country, these concerns are not theoretical, they're personal: 46 percent of Americans report being somewhat or very concerned that ICE could mistreat someone they know. This is clearly the kind of playing field in which a fight--which will drive further attention towards ICE's abuses--is politically advantageous.
Grassroots Democrats understand this, and over the last week they have been intensely ramping up [pressure](https://substack.com/redirect/98998b93-e8e7-404d-9bd1-436f884fd8c1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on their Congressional leaders. The good news is that this uproar is having a serious impact. Just this morning, House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries [told](https://substack.com/redirect/a2205f5c-c527-4103-8822-ea47a69d49b4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) his colleagues that he will be voting no on the bill to fund the Department of Homeland Security, and it seems like House Democrats are overwhelmingly coming together to oppose the deal. That leaves the Senate, where--unlike in the House--Republicans will need Democratic support to reach the 60 votes necessary to pass their Gestapo funding bill.
Some Democratic senators have already made clear they're on the right side of this fight. For example, Connecticut senator Chris Murphy [announced](https://substack.com/redirect/c04a0a61-8977-4f52-83ee-7a078d8b228b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg):
> The proposed Appropriations bill for the Department of Homeland Security released today puts no meaningful constraints on the growing lawlessness of ICE, and increases funding for detention over the last Appropriations bill passed in 2024. ... Democrats have no obligation to support a bill that not only funds the dystopian scenes we are seeing in Minneapolis but will allow DHS to replicate that playbook of brutality in cities all over this country.
But other Democrats, like Washington senator [Patty Murra](https://substack.com/redirect/6c16255d-9c2f-41e4-a726-e32edd02490d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)y, have been pushing for passage of the deal, and it seems highly unlikely that Democratic leadership (I'm looking at you, Chuck "folds every time" Schumer) will whip the caucus to stand in united opposition to this legislation.
It would be terribly dispiriting to see Senate Democrats cede what is likely their last concrete opportunity this year to block the appropriations that are funding ICE's horrific abuses. And such a failure would strike a particularly stark contrast between those Democratic leaders who are not rising to the occasion, and the actual people of Minnesota, and all across the country, who _**absolutely are**_.
In the weeks since ICE began its assault on Minneapolis, the solidarity with which Minnesotans have responded has been extraordinary. We've seen thousands of regular people organizing--sometimes through established activist channels, but as often as not [through](https://substack.com/redirect/840cea0f-c373-4b6a-8153-6d64dd2e1081?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) churches, neighborhood group chats, and school Facebook groups--to stand up to Trump's attacks on their neighbors. They're following ICE officers across the city, honking horns, blowing whistles, recording abductions, and nonviolently disrupting these fascist operations however they can. Other community members are [mobilizing](https://substack.com/redirect/5d8e07bf-0a5f-4630-a9e7-67fe8d492a29?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to deliver groceries and offer rides to migrants who are afraid to leave their homes.
It's among the most beautiful examples of real-life antifascism I have ever seen. And it's why, as deeply horrifying as these last few weeks have been, I am actually, right now, feeling more optimistic about the survival of American democracy than I have in a long time. Over the last year we've seen practically every elite institution--corporations, law firms, universities, the Democratic establishment--bend the knee to Trump. But regular people all across the country--the people with the most to lose, who are the least insulated against the consequences of their resistance--have consistently refused to give in.
This is where we must look to for our salvation. It's in our relationships with our communities, our love for our neighbors, and our hatred of bullies. There's a suffocating amount of malice and evil out there right now. But there's also a tremendous amount of good old-fashioned American moxie, compassion, and stubbornness. As fragile and corrupt as our elite institutions have revealed themselves to be, the American public--the regular people of this country--are proving themselves remarkably resilient to Trump's authoritarianism. This record should not only inform our strategies of resistance moving forward--it should also provide us with a durable source of hope as we look down the barrel of three increasingly dark and dangerous years.
For more strategies of resistance and durable sources of hope, subscribe here!

body:
I’d like to count on your support right now.
#
Hi Peter —
I know I ask for your help a lot, and I know a donation might not always fit in your budget. **I do not expect you to give every time I ask.**
In fact, only a fraction of people give to any of our emails — but they remain the best way for us to connect with the supporters who are powering our work, so we really value each one! **[I am asking you to give today (even a small donation will help) not because I want to, but because I have to. If you’re with me already, can I count you in to split a contribution between our campaign and State Democrats Committee before our January deadline?](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/99947?refcode=em20260121-9970&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=1&akid=9970%2E614464%2Ef2B7DC)**
The fact is, the GOP’s attention is on us. They see our campaign as the biggest threat to their Senate majority, so they have far-right PACs and mega-donors lined up to pour money into North Carolina on behalf of our MAGA opponents.

| | Let’s set the scene: It’s January. The beginning of a midterm election year. Tons of wins in 2025 elections show — we could see a wave election where control of Congress flips. And the Supreme Court is poised to upend the rules of the game. We’re talking about January 21, 2010 — 16 years ago today, when five right-wing justices ruled that corporations could spend unlimited sums to elect politicians who would do their bidding. The case? _Citizens United v. FEC_ , of course. Now, at the start of another critical midterm election year, the Supreme Court looks ready to hit our democracy with another major decision in _Louisiana v. Callais._ If they gut Section 2 of the Voting Rights Act, Republican state legislatures could draw new racially discriminatory voting maps — and many are openly preparing to do so. Those new maps could deprive Black and brown Americans of any real chance at electing the candidates of their choice in hundreds of congressional and state legislative districts. And depending on the timing of the ruling, new maps could be in effect this November. In both _Citizens United_ and _Callais_ , the Supreme Court took the rare step of asking for a case to be re-argued — a typical indicator that a landmark ruling could be on the way. And _Callais_ could follow in _Citizens United’s_ footsteps by once again making it harder for voters to make their voices heard in our democracy — once again allowing politicians and their wealthy donors to consolidate their own power without worrying about true accountability from the American people. **If we could go back in time to before the _Citizens United_ ruling, we’d do everything we could to shore up our democracy against corporate control. In both Citizens United and Callais , the Supreme Court took the rare step of asking for a case to be re-argued — a typical indicator that a landmark ruling could be on the way. And Callais could follow in Citizens United’s footsteps by once again making it harder for voters to make their voices heard in our democracy — once again allowing politicians and their wealthy donors to consolidate their own power without worrying about true accountability from the American people. If we could go back in time to before the Citizens United ruling, we’d do everything we could to shore up our democracy against corporate control. We don’t have a time machine — but we can, and must, act now before another potentially devastating ruling. At Fair Fight, we’re prepared to defend free and fair elections from the damage the Supreme Court may be about to inflict: we’re ready to push back against the MAGA takeover by electing state-level Democracy Champions who can help stop harmful new maps. = If you've saved payment info with ActBlue Express, your donation will process automatically: | = | = ---|--- = | = ---|--- = | = ---|--- In solidarity, The Fair Fight Team * = = | 1270 Caroline Street | Suite D120-430 | Atlanta, GA 30307 ©2026 Fair Fight - All rights reserved. Idaho's got licensing boards for everything...

Some are sitting on millions of dollars in reserves and others are underwater by over -120%.

So today in Senate H&W committee, a few failing boards proposed doubling fees (some wanted increases over 100%).

The boards are insolvent because they're poorly managed. Or because maybe they shouldn't exist in the first place. So their answer is to squeeze practitioners harder? Make them cough up double to fund bureaucrats who add zero value?

Nope. The real answer is elimination. Get rid of useless licensing boards entirely and let the free market work.

If someone's bad at their job, word gets around. Customers figure it out. We don't need a committee sitting on millions in reserves while another one drowns in debt, all while charging people thousands just for permission to work.

One testifier got asked what it was like doing acupuncture before licensing in Idhao existed. Her answer?

**"Everyone was fine and did great work."**

We had a functioning market. Then government showed up and demanded permission slips for a problem that didn't exist.

**" Winter storm watch issued for North Texas warns of dangerous cold and ice"** via [Dallas Morning News](https://substack.com/redirect/4e65ad59-562e-448a-ac72-b7994e25d08c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) - A winter storm watch has been issued by the National Weather Service for Dallas-Fort Worth, with impacts coming late this week and into the weekend.

The alert warns of hazardous winter weather, including snow, ice and freezing temperatures, in all of North and much of Central Texas. Freezing precipitation is expected to start Friday afternoon and continue through Saturday night.

"Dangerous" cold is also expected to last through Monday morning, with temperatures forecast to drop to the single digits overnight in some parts of the region. Temperatures are not expected to rise above 32 degrees at DFW International Airport from 6 p.m. Friday until Monday afternoon.

**Greg Abbott** also activated the state's emergency response resources on Tuesday ahead of the winter weather threat. The move includes directing the Texas Department of Transportation to pretreat roads, as well as instructing several other departments to have additional personnel ready to assist with road closures.

(_[DMN](https://substack.com/redirect/19f8c9e1-a30c-46a1-b5ee-485110c3c8b1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_)
**" Cold front could bring ice, snow to Texas. Here's what to expect"** via [Houston Chronicle](https://substack.com/redirect/fcc28066-676b-4cd4-8669-e0771f5b40f5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) - A potentially hazardous winter storm is about three to four days away, so weather forecasts can still change significantly until then. However, here's what we know so far about timing, temperatures, and types of winter precipitation that are possible across the state of Texas.

The arctic cold front is expected to start pushing through North Texas by early Friday morning, likely reaching Central and West Texas by noon. It will continue south, bringing cold air toward Austin, San Antonio and Houston by early Friday evening.

Models indicate a bitter cold day Saturday for much of the state. Most areas across the northern half of the state will stay significantly below freezing throughout the afternoon, with highs in the 20s around the Dallas-Fort Worth area. For those in South Texas, subfreezing daytime high temps are less likely, but afternoon temps will still struggle to rise out of the 30s.

With the amount of cold air indicated by weather models, as well as a steady stream of Pacific moisture from the west, confidence is increasing that much of the state will see wintry precipitation, some of which could be heavy.

(_[HOU CHRON](https://substack.com/redirect/fcc28066-676b-4cd4-8669-e0771f5b40f5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_)

**" Autopsy finds Cuban immigrant in ICE custody died of homicide due to asphyxia"** via [AP](https://substack.com/redirect/c5428f21-c43d-411f-a6ee-d319ab97f5d6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) - A Cuban migrant held in solitary confinement at an immigration detention facility in Texas died after guards held him down and he stopped breathing, according to an autopsy report released Wednesday that ruled the death a homicide.

**Geraldo Lunas Campos** died Jan. 3 following an altercation with guards. U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement said the 55-year-old father of four was attempting suicide and the staff tried to save him.
[BECOME A PAID SUBSCRIBER: $70/yr](https://substack.com/redirect/d93b6796-01ae-476d-9720-3cdfffd35a47?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
But a witness [told The Associated Press](https://substack.com/redirect/225a9fe0-660d-496a-86c5-15a53c5c4e86?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) last week that **Lunas Campos** was handcuffed as at least five guards held him down and one put an arm around his neck and squeezed until he was unconscious.

His death was one of at least three reported in little more than a month at Camp East Montana, a sprawling tent facility in the desert on the grounds of Fort Bliss, an Army base.

The autopsy report by the El Paso County Medical Examiner's Office found Lunas Campos' body showed signs of a struggle, including abrasions on his chest and knees. He also had hemorrhages on his neck. The deputy medical examiner, Dr. **Adam Gonzalez**. determined the cause of death was asphyxia due to neck and torso compression.

The report said witnesses saw Lunas Campos "become unresponsive while being physically restrained by law enforcement." It did not elaborate on what happened during the struggle but cited evidence of injuries to his neck, head and torso associated with physical restraint. The report also noted the presence of petechial hemorrhages -- tiny blood spots from burst capillaries that can be associated with intense strain or injury -- in the eyelids and skin of the neck.

Dr. **Victor Weedn** , a forensic pathologist who reviewed the autopsy report for AP, said the presence of petechiae in the eyes support the conclusion that asphyxia caused the death. Those injuries suggest pressure on the body and are often associated with such deaths, he said.

He said the contusions on Lunas Campos' body may reflect physical restraint and the neck injuries were consistent with a hand or knee on the neck.

The autopsy also found the presence of prescription antidepressant and antihistamine medications, adding that Lunas Campos had a history of bipolar disorder and anxiety. It made no mention of him attempting suicide.

([AP](https://substack.com/redirect/c5428f21-c43d-411f-a6ee-d319ab97f5d6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))

* **STATE GOVERNMENT**

**" ERCOT: Texas power grid is ready ahead of incoming winter storm"** via [Texas Public Radio](https://substack.com/redirect/3d9fff11-769f-4a42-8d9b-e9e87f676260?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) - Texas grid officials say the state is prepared to meet electricity demand ahead of a powerful winter storm that's expected to bring days of freezing temperatures and the chance of ice or snow across parts of the state later this week.

The Electric Reliability Council of Texas, which oversees the state's power grid, told The Texas Newsroom on Tuesday that based on expected weather conditions, it "anticipates there will be sufficient generation to meet demand" ahead of the storm.

"ERCOT will continue to deploy all available resources to manage the grid reliably and coordinate closely with the Public Utility Commission, generation providers, and transmission utilities," the council said in a statement.

Subfreezing temperatures are forecast to arrive by Friday as arctic air pushes south into Texas. Forecasters say moisture arriving late Friday night into Saturday could set the stage for hazardous winter weather throughout the state.

(_TPR_)
* * *
* **LOCAL GOVERNMENT**

**" Grapevine-Colleyville ISD High School Receives Backlash for Hosting CAIR-Sponsored 'Islamic Games'"** [The Texan's](https://substack.com/redirect/86cc9be3-44ec-4245-810d-4c3cf24bbfd3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) **Meridith Dyer** - Colleyville Heritage High School, part of Grapevine-Colleyville Independent School District (ISD), is scheduled to host the Dallas Islamic Games on May 9 and 10, 2026.

According to the Islamic Games website, the event is North America's largest Muslim sports and athletic event and is "dedicated to promoting physical excellence, unity, and community development."

(_[THE TEXAN](https://substack.com/redirect/0a4fad64-fd10-48bd-86e5-c985353a4dfe?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_)

**" Bexar County now allows contracts up to $100K to go without court approval"** [San Antonio Report's](https://substack.com/redirect/b893a5e3-6957-4f68-b032-54a733cdec7f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) **Andrea Drusch** - Bexar County Commissioners Court is embracing a new policy that gives county department heads authority to make purchases up to $100,000 without coming before the elected leaders for approval. The change was made possible during the last Texas legislative session, and the five-member Commissioners Court largely agreed Tuesday they should make the change -- given the amount of frustration they've heard surrounding slow-moving contracts.

"Hopefully what we'll see in return is a more effective and efficient process of executing contracts and the procurement process, which has always been a prior criticism," Bexar County **Judge Peter Sakai** said of the new policy. " ... We can move very fast as county government. We don't have to have that, 'Well, the county takes [forever].'"

Earlier that morning, a voter registration vendor seeking to work with the county came before the court to air grievances about the process.

(_[SA REPORT](https://substack.com/redirect/433d8a8a-b95a-4f6c-89b0-c5a8c5600440?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_)
* * *
* **2026**

**" Gov. Abbott endorses Nate Sheets over Sid Miller for agriculture commissioner**," [Texas Tribune's](https://substack.com/redirect/0bf442f2-688e-4a9a-b788-8ff2c56fee52?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**Kate McGee** \-- In a stunning blow to Texas Agriculture Commissioner **Sid Miller** , Gov. **Greg Abbott** endorsed Miller's Republican primary challenger for agriculture commissioner, putting his support behind first-time political candidate **Nate Sheets**.

"Texans deserve an Agriculture Commissioner who is focused on promoting Texas Agriculture, with zero tolerance for criminality," Abbott wrote Wednesday on social media. "Nate Sheets is the true conservative champion for the job and is the leader we need to keep Texas the global powerhouse in agriculture."

Last year, Miller turned heads when he hired his political consultant **Todd Smith** as the agency's chief of staff just a few months after [Smith pleaded guilty to commercial bribery](https://substack.com/redirect/cc700563-87aa-4dad-8842-86f0f80d1788?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) after he was criminally charged for selling hemp licenses that are regulated by Miller's office. The move sparked outrage among agency employees [who told Texas Rangers](https://substack.com/redirect/2f8dfb60-d5a7-48dd-8770-c11fc69c94fb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) they had warned Miller about Smith.

Miller did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

In a statement, Sheets said: "I'm honored to have Governor Abbott's support and I look forward to working together to fight for Texas agriculture and for farmers' and ranchers' future economic success, restore trust in our food system, and ensure Texas remains strong, healthy, and secure for generations to come."

Sheets is the founder of Nature Nate's Honey company. A native Texan business and ranch owner, he served for six years in the U.S. Naval Reserve before graduating from Texas State University. Sheets sold Nature Nate's in 2021 and resigned as CEO in 2024 to run for agriculture commissioner. He also previously worked as communications director for E3 Partners, an evangelist ministry that establishes new Christian congregations around the world.

In a statement, **Kim Snyder** , Abbott's campaign manager, said Abbott endorsed Sheets because of Miller's "history of corruption" and pointed to [his vote in favor of in-state tuition for undocumented students](https://substack.com/redirect/c5345675-266f-4a6e-9adf-6d007673f858?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) when Miller served in the Texas House. At the time, the measure had broad bipartisan support, but as the Republican Party has shifted further to the right, it has become a political sticking point among hardline anti-immigrant politicians.

"Nate Sheets is the only candidate in the race who has the integrity to lead the Texas Department of Agriculture," Snyder added.

([Texas Tribune](https://substack.com/redirect/0bf442f2-688e-4a9a-b788-8ff2c56fee52?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))

**" Rep. James Talarico takes lead in Democratic Texas Senate primary poll"** via [El Paso Times](https://substack.com/redirect/d4eb5070-1190-42e3-88d7-18a34c809672?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) - New polling shows state Rep. **James Talarico** leading the Democratic 2026 primary race for a Texas U.S. Senate seat.

A new poll from Emerson College Polling and Nexstar Media shows Talarico, D-Austin, earning support from 47% of possible primary voters compared to 38% for U.S. Rep. **Jasmine Crockett** , D-Dallas, and 15% still undecided.

"Talarico has built momentum among Hispanic (59%) and white (57%) voters, while a majority of Black Democratic primary voters (80%) support Crockett," **Spencer Kimball** , executive director of Emerson College Polling, noted in a news release. "Men also break for Talarico 52% to 30%, while women are about evenly split between the two Democrats, 44% for Talarico and 43% for Crockett."

A head-to-head matchup between either of the leading Republican primary Senate candidates -- incumbent U.S. Sen. **John Cornyn** and Texas Attorney General **Ken Paxton** -- shows Talarico and Crockett fairing about the same.

(_[EP TIMES](https://substack.com/redirect/d089818c-d2db-4a23-9213-e40aded38dfb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_)

**" Beto O'Rourke won't endorse in Texas Senate Democratic primary"** via [Dallas Morning News](https://substack.com/redirect/18a7dbdd-3ce6-49a8-9a57-d778ba4f36e8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) - **Beto O 'Rourke** says he will not make an endorsement in the Democratic primary for Senate, calling U.S. Rep. **Jasmine Crockett** and state Rep. **James Talarico** "generational talents" who have what it takes to win.

"I believe in the Democratic voters of the state of Texas, who are going to have a real close and personal look at these two phenomenal candidates," armed with appealing messages, fundraising skills and media presence, O'Rourke told Hearst Newspapers.

Crockett and Talarico square off in the March 3 primary.

Instead of picking a side, O'Rourke said he will focus on his Powered By People political action committee. He said that's aimed especially at young voters and relies on more personal engagement to boost turnout for the eventual nominee.

"We're going to make sure we have enough net new Democratic voters who aren't just on the rolls, but are engaged, involved, informed and turn out to vote," O'Rourke said.

(_[DMN](https://substack.com/redirect/a6b4a3e3-91cf-4b00-8110-0a60eb77bdce?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_)

**" A former MLB star is a frontrunner for TX-21. Critics say he's buying a seat."** [San Antonio Express-News's](https://substack.com/redirect/285249cc-bf84-43f2-9311-8746084b20f0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) **Bayliss Wagner** - He's never held elected office and only once voted in a Republican primary. For most of his adult life, he lived far from Texas, building a standout baseball career.

**Mark "Tex" Teixeira** might not fit the mold of a traditional candidate, but he has quickly emerged as a frontrunner in the race to succeed U.S. Rep. Chip Roy, R-Austin, in Congress.

Teixeira is dominating the Republican primary for Texas' 21st Congressional District in cash on hand, loaning roughly $2 million to his own campaign and raising another $500,000 -- far beyond the funds reported so far by his opponents. He also has high-profile endorsements from Gov. **Greg Abbott** and 11 sitting members of Congress, among them House Majority Whip**Steve Scalise** and nine Texans.

Teixeira has sought to portray himself as an analog to President Donald Trump -- a political outsider who's focused on tightening immigration rules, cutting "waste, fraud and abuse" and keeping "biological men out of our girls' sports."

"I've been on a lot of great teams, and President Trump's team is one I want to be on to secure the border and crush the cartels," he said in a TV ad.

(_[SAEN](https://substack.com/redirect/285249cc-bf84-43f2-9311-8746084b20f0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_)

TOP NEWS " Winter storm watch issued for North Texas warns of dangerous cold and ice" via - A winter storm watch has been issued by the National Weather Service for Dallas-Fort Worth, with impacts coming late this week and into the weekend. The alert warns of hazardous winter weather, including snow, ice and freezing temperatures, in all of North and much of Central Texas. Freezing precipitation is expected to start Friday afternoon and continue through Saturday night. "Dangerous" cold is also expected to last through Monday morning, with temperatures forecast to drop to the single digits overnight in some parts of the region. Temperatures are not expected to rise above 32 degrees at DFW International Airport from 6 p.m. Friday until Monday afternoon. Greg Abbott also activated the state's emergency response resources on Tuesday ahead of the winter weather threat. The move includes directing the Texas Department of Transportation to pretreat roads, as well as instructing several other departments to have additional personnel ready to assist with road closures. () " Cold front could bring ice, snow to Texas. Here's what to expect" via - A potentially hazardous winter storm is about three to four days away, so weather forecasts can still change significantly until then. However, here's what we know so far about timing, temperatures, and types of winter precipitation that are possible across the state of Texas. The arctic cold front is expected to start pushing through North Texas by early Friday morning, likely reaching Central and West Texas by noon. It will continue south, bringing cold air toward Austin, San Antonio and Houston by early Friday evening. Models indicate a bitter cold day Saturday for much of the state. Most areas across the northern half of the state will stay significantly below freezing throughout the afternoon, with highs in the 20s around the Dallas-Fort Worth area. For those in South Texas, subfreezing daytime high temps are less likely, but afternoon temps will still struggle to rise out of the 30s. With the amount of cold air indicated by weather models, as well as a steady stream of Pacific moisture from the west, confidence is increasing that much of the state will see wintry precipitation, some of which could be heavy. () " Autopsy finds Cuban immigrant in ICE custody died of homicide due to asphyxia" via - A Cuban migrant held in solitary confinement at an immigration detention facility in Texas died after guards held him down and he stopped breathing, according to an autopsy report released Wednesday that ruled the death a homicide. Geraldo Lunas Campos died Jan. 3 following an altercation with guards. U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement said the 55-year-old father of four was attempting suicide and the staff tried to save him. But a witness last week that Lunas Campos was handcuffed as at least five guards held him down and one put an arm around his neck and squeezed until he was unconscious. His death was one of at least three reported in little more than a month at Camp East Montana, a sprawling tent facility in the desert on the grounds of Fort Bliss, an Army base. The autopsy report by the El Paso County Medical Examiner's Office found Lunas Campos' body showed signs of a struggle, including abrasions on his chest and knees. He also had hemorrhages on his neck. The deputy medical examiner, Dr. Adam Gonzalez. determined the cause of death was asphyxia due to neck and torso compression. The report said witnesses saw Lunas Campos "become unresponsive while being physically restrained by law enforcement." It did not elaborate on what happened during the struggle but cited evidence of injuries to his neck, head and torso associated with physical restraint. The report also noted the presence of petechial hemorrhages -- tiny blood spots from burst capillaries that can be associated with intense strain or injury -- in the eyelids and skin of the neck. Dr. Victor Weedn , a forensic pathologist who reviewed the autopsy report for AP, said the presence of petechiae in the eyes support the conclusion that asphyxia caused the death. Those injuries suggest pressure on the body and are often associated with such deaths, he said. He said the contusions on Lunas Campos' body may reflect physical restraint and the neck injuries were consistent with a hand or knee on the neck. The autopsy also found the presence of prescription antidepressant and antihistamine medications, adding that Lunas Campos had a history of bipolar disorder and anxiety. It made no mention of him attempting suicide. () STATE GOVERNMENT " ERCOT: Texas power grid is ready ahead of incoming winter storm" via - Texas grid officials say the state is prepared to meet electricity demand ahead of a powerful winter storm that's expected to bring days of freezing temperatures and the chance of ice or snow across parts of the state later this week. The Electric Reliability Council of Texas, which oversees the state's power grid, told The Texas Newsroom on Tuesday that based on expected weather conditions, it "anticipates there will be sufficient generation to meet demand" ahead of the storm. "ERCOT will continue to deploy all available resources to manage the grid reliably and coordinate closely with the Public Utility Commission, generation providers, and transmission utilities," the council said in a statement. Subfreezing temperatures are forecast to arrive by Friday as arctic air pushes south into Texas. Forecasters say moisture arriving late Friday night into Saturday could set the stage for hazardous winter weather throughout the state. (TPR) LOCAL GOVERNMENT " Grapevine-Colleyville ISD High School Receives Backlash for Hosting CAIR-Sponsored 'Islamic Games'" Meridith Dyer - Colleyville Heritage High School, part of Grapevine-Colleyville Independent School District (ISD), is scheduled to host the Dallas Islamic Games on May 9 and 10, 2026. According to the Islamic Games website, the event is North America's largest Muslim sports and athletic event and is "dedicated to promoting physical excellence, unity, and community development." () " Bexar County now allows contracts up to $100K to go without court approval" Andrea Drusch - Bexar County Commissioners Court is embracing a new policy that gives county department heads authority to make purchases up to $100,000 without coming before the elected leaders for approval. The change was made possible during the last Texas legislative session, and the five-member Commissioners Court largely agreed Tuesday they should make the change -- given the amount of frustration they've heard surrounding slow-moving contracts. "Hopefully what we'll see in return is a more effective and efficient process of executing contracts and the procurement process, which has always been a prior criticism," Bexar County Judge Peter Sakai said of the new policy. " ... We can move very fast as county government. We don't have to have that, 'Well, the county takes [forever].'" Earlier that morning, a voter registration vendor seeking to work with the county came before the court to air grievances about the process. () 2026 " Gov. Abbott endorses Nate Sheets over Sid Miller for agriculture commissioner," McGee \-- In a stunning blow to Texas Agriculture Commissioner Sid Miller , Gov. Greg Abbott endorsed Miller's Republican primary challenger for agriculture commissioner, putting his support behind first-time political candidate Nate Sheets. "Texans deserve an Agriculture Commissioner who is focused on promoting Texas Agriculture, with zero tolerance for criminality," Abbott wrote Wednesday on social media. "Nate Sheets is the true conservative champion for the job and is the leader we need to keep Texas the global powerhouse in agriculture." Last year, Miller turned heads when he hired his political consultant Todd Smith as the agency's chief of staff just a few months after after he was criminally charged for selling hemp licenses that are regulated by Miller's office. The move sparked outrage among agency employees they had warned Miller about Smith. Miller did not immediately respond to a request for comment. In a statement, Sheets said: "I'm honored to have Governor Abbott's support and I look forward to working together to fight for Texas agriculture and for farmers' and ranchers' future economic success, restore trust in our food system, and ensure Texas remains strong, healthy, and secure for generations to come." Sheets is the founder of Nature Nate's Honey company. A native Texan business and ranch owner, he served for six years in the U.S. Naval Reserve before graduating from Texas State University. Sheets sold Nature Nate's in 2021 and resigned as CEO in 2024 to run for agriculture commissioner. He also previously worked as communications director for E3 Partners, an evangelist ministry that establishes new Christian congregations around the world. In a statement, Kim Snyder , Abbott's campaign manager, said Abbott endorsed Sheets because of Miller's "history of corruption" and pointed to when Miller served in the Texas House. At the time, the measure had broad bipartisan support, but as the Republican Party has shifted further to the right, it has become a political sticking point among hardline anti-immigrant politicians. "Nate Sheets is the only candidate in the race who has the integrity to lead the Texas Department of Agriculture," Snyder added. () " Rep. James Talarico takes lead in Democratic Texas Senate primary poll" via - New polling shows state Rep. James Talarico leading the Democratic 2026 primary race for a Texas U.S. Senate seat. A new poll from Emerson College Polling and Nexstar Media shows Talarico, D-Austin, earning support from 47% of possible primary voters compared to 38% for U.S. Rep. Jasmine Crockett , D-Dallas, and 15% still undecided. "Talarico has built momentum among Hispanic (59%) and white (57%) voters, while a majority of Black Democratic primary voters (80%) support Crockett," Spencer Kimball , executive director of Emerson College Polling, noted in a news release. "Men also break for Talarico 52% to 30%, while women are about evenly split between the two Democrats, 44% for Talarico and 43% for Crockett." A head-to-head matchup between either of the leading Republican primary Senate candidates -- incumbent U.S. Sen. John Cornyn and Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton -- shows Talarico and Crockett fairing about the same. () " Beto O'Rourke won't endorse in Texas Senate Democratic primary" via - Beto O 'Rourke says he will not make an endorsement in the Democratic primary for Senate, calling U.S. Rep. Jasmine Crockett and state Rep. James Talarico "generational talents" who have what it takes to win. "I believe in the Democratic voters of the state of Texas, who are going to have a real close and personal look at these two phenomenal candidates," armed with appealing messages, fundraising skills and media presence, O'Rourke told Hearst Newspapers. Crockett and Talarico square off in the March 3 primary. Instead of picking a side, O'Rourke said he will focus on his Powered By People political action committee. He said that's aimed especially at young voters and relies on more personal engagement to boost turnout for the eventual nominee. "We're going to make sure we have enough net new Democratic voters who aren't just on the rolls, but are engaged, involved, informed and turn out to vote," O'Rourke said. () " A former MLB star is a frontrunner for TX-21. Critics say he's buying a seat." Bayliss Wagner - He's never held elected office and only once voted in a Republican primary. For most of his adult life, he lived far from Texas, building a standout baseball career. Mark "Tex" Teixeira might not fit the mold of a traditional candidate, but he has quickly emerged as a frontrunner in the race to succeed U.S. Rep. Chip Roy, R-Austin, in Congress. Teixeira is dominating the Republican primary for Texas' 21st Congressional District in cash on hand, loaning roughly $2 million to his own campaign and raising another $500,000 -- far beyond the funds reported so far by his opponents. He also has high-profile endorsements from Gov. Greg Abbott and 11 sitting members of Congress, among them House Majority WhipSteve Scalise and nine Texans. Teixeira has sought to portray himself as an analog to President Donald Trump -- a political outsider who's focused on tightening immigration rules, cutting "waste, fraud and abuse" and keeping "biological men out of our girls' sports." "I've been on a lot of great teams, and President Trump's team is one I want to be on to secure the border and crush the cartels," he said in a TV ad. **" Winter storm watch issued for North Texas warns of dangerous cold and ice"** via [Dallas Morning News](https://substack.com/redirect/2667bec6-b2c2-4938-97c6-93b3a6c55d7e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) - A winter storm watch has been issued by the National Weather Service for Dallas-Fort Worth, with impacts coming late this week and into the weekend.

The alert warns of hazardous winter weather, including snow, ice and freezing temperatures, in all of North and much of Central Texas. Freezing precipitation is expected to start Friday afternoon and continue through Saturday night.

"Dangerous" cold is also expected to last through Monday morning, with temperatures forecast to drop to the single digits overnight in some parts of the region. Temperatures are not expected to rise above 32 degrees at DFW International Airport from 6 p.m. Friday until Monday afternoon.

**Greg Abbott** also activated the state's emergency response resources on Tuesday ahead of the winter weather threat. The move includes directing the Texas Department of Transportation to pretreat roads, as well as instructing several other departments to have additional personnel ready to assist with road closures.

(_[DMN](https://substack.com/redirect/ff45a543-7fc2-457c-b024-a20d15236ec8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_)

**" Autopsy finds Cuban immigrant in ICE custody died of homicide due to asphyxia"** via [AP](https://substack.com/redirect/5e8a60f9-dda9-4d0c-a4e2-6db16ed8ceea?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) - A Cuban migrant held in solitary confinement at an immigration detention facility in Texas died after guards held him down and he stopped breathing, according to an autopsy report released Wednesday that ruled the death a homicide.

**Geraldo Lunas Campos** died Jan. 3 following an altercation with guards. U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement said the 55-year-old father of four was attempting suicide and the staff tried to save him.

But a witness [told The Associated Press](https://substack.com/redirect/fdf30b0a-b421-4f0d-b3bc-c0db80124002?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) last week that **Lunas Campos** was handcuffed as at least five guards held him down and one put an arm around his neck and squeezed until he was unconscious.

His death was one of at least three reported in little more than a month at Camp East Montana, a sprawling tent facility in the desert on the grounds of Fort Bliss, an Army base.

The autopsy report by the El Paso County Medical Examiner's Office found Lunas Campos' body showed signs of a struggle, including abrasions on his chest and knees. He also had hemorrhages on his neck. The deputy medical examiner, Dr. **Adam Gonzalez**. determined the cause of death was asphyxia due to neck and torso compression.

The report said witnesses saw Lunas Campos "become unresponsive while being physically restrained by law enforcement." It did not elaborate on what happened during the struggle but cited evidence of injuries to his neck, head and torso associated with physical restraint. The report also noted the presence of petechial hemorrhages -- tiny blood spots from burst capillaries that can be associated with intense strain or injury -- in the eyelids and skin of the neck.

Dr. **Victor Weedn** , a forensic pathologist who reviewed the autopsy report for AP, said the presence of petechiae in the eyes support the conclusion that asphyxia caused the death. Those injuries suggest pressure on the body and are often associated with such deaths, he said.

He said the contusions on Lunas Campos' body may reflect physical restraint and the neck injuries were consistent with a hand or knee on the neck.

The autopsy also found the presence of prescription antidepressant and antihistamine medications, adding that Lunas Campos had a history of bipolar disorder and anxiety. It made no mention of him attempting suicide.

**" ERCOT: Texas power grid is ready ahead of incoming winter storm"** via [Texas Public Radio](https://substack.com/redirect/4cccb95e-8ffb-4555-9b49-8e1a3fdf8d65?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) - Texas grid officials say the state is prepared to meet electricity demand ahead of a powerful winter storm that's expected to bring days of freezing temperatures and the chance of ice or snow across parts of the state later this week.

The Electric Reliability Council of Texas, which oversees the state's power grid, told The Texas Newsroom on Tuesday that based on expected weather conditions, it "anticipates there will be sufficient generation to meet demand" ahead of the storm.

"ERCOT will continue to deploy all available resources to manage the grid reliably and coordinate closely with the Public Utility Commission, generation providers, and transmission utilities," the council said in a statement.

Subfreezing temperatures are forecast to arrive by Friday as arctic air pushes south into Texas. Forecasters say moisture arriving late Friday night into Saturday could set the stage for hazardous winter weather throughout the state.

* **2026**

**" Gov. Abbott endorses Nate Sheets over Sid Miller for agriculture commissioner**," [Texas Tribune's](https://substack.com/redirect/e0a797d6-35c2-4801-ac8f-4abf797555d6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**Kate McGee** \-- In a stunning blow to Texas Agriculture Commissioner **Sid Miller** , Gov. **Greg Abbott** endorsed Miller's Republican primary challenger for agriculture commissioner, putting his support behind first-time political candidate **Nate Sheets**.

"Texans deserve an Agriculture Commissioner who is focused on promoting Texas Agriculture, with zero tolerance for criminality," Abbott wrote Wednesday on social media. "Nate Sheets is the true conservative champion for the job and is the leader we need to keep Texas the global powerhouse in agriculture."

Last year, Miller turned heads when he hired his political consultant **Todd Smith** as the agency's chief of staff just a few months after [Smith pleaded guilty to commercial bribery](https://substack.com/redirect/779dc2e2-6bfb-4c0a-b233-c8e313132425?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) after he was criminally charged for selling hemp licenses that are regulated by Miller's office. The move sparked outrage among agency employees [who told Texas Rangers](https://substack.com/redirect/88fe037e-7d9f-48c8-bc51-104e7002a84e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) they had warned Miller about Smith.

Miller did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

In a statement, Sheets said: "I'm honored to have Governor Abbott's support and I look forward to working together to fight for Texas agriculture and for farmers' and ranchers' future economic success, restore trust in our food system, and ensure Texas remains strong, healthy, and secure for generations to come."

Sheets is the founder of Nature Nate's Honey company. A native Texan business and ranch owner, he served for six years in the U.S. Naval Reserve before graduating from Texas State University. Sheets sold Nature Nate's in 2021 and resigned as CEO in 2024 to run for agriculture commissioner. He also previously worked as communications director for E3 Partners, an evangelist ministry that establishes new Christian congregations around the world.

In a statement, **Kim Snyder** , Abbott's campaign manager, said Abbott endorsed Sheets because of Miller's "history of corruption" and pointed to [his vote in favor of in-state tuition for undocumented students](https://substack.com/redirect/edba138d-4631-49b6-b7cc-3a66b0c99c9b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) when Miller served in the Texas House. At the time, the measure had broad bipartisan support, but as the Republican Party has shifted further to the right, it has become a political sticking point among hardline anti-immigrant politicians.

"Nate Sheets is the only candidate in the race who has the integrity to lead the Texas Department of Agriculture," Snyder added.

([Texas Tribune](https://substack.com/redirect/e0a797d6-35c2-4801-ac8f-4abf797555d6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))

A new poll from Emerson College Polling and Nexstar Media shows Talarico, D-Austin, earning support from 47% of possible primary voters compared to 38% for U.S. Rep. **Jasmine Crockett** , D-Dallas, and 15% still undecided.

"Talarico has built momentum among Hispanic (59%) and white (57%) voters, while a majority of Black Democratic primary voters (80%) support Crockett," **Spencer Kimball** , executive director of Emerson College Polling, noted in a news release. "Men also break for Talarico 52% to 30%, while women are about evenly split between the two Democrats, 44% for Talarico and 43% for Crockett."

A head-to-head matchup between either of the leading Republican primary Senate candidates -- incumbent U.S. Sen. **John Cornyn** and Texas Attorney General **Ken Paxton** -- shows Talarico and Crockett fairing about the same.

However, here's what we know so far about timing, temperatures, and types of winter precipitation that are possible across the state of Texas. The arctic cold front is expected to start pushing through North Texas by early Friday morning, likely reaching Central and West Texas by noon. () " Autopsy finds Cuban immigrant in ICE custody died of homicide due to asphyxia" via - A Cuban migrant held in solitary confinement at an immigration detention facility in Texas died after guards held him down and he stopped breathing, according to an autopsy report released Wednesday that ruled the death a homicide. Geraldo Lunas Campos died Jan. 3 following an altercation with guards. U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement said the 55-year-old father of four was attempting suicide and the staff tried to save him. But a witness last week that Lunas Campos was handcuffed as at least five guards held him down and one put an arm around his neck and squeezed until he was unconscious. His death was one of at least three reported in little more than a month at Camp East Montana, a sprawling tent facility in the desert on the grounds of Fort Bliss, an Army base. The autopsy report by the El Paso County Medical Examiner's Office found Lunas Campos' body showed signs of a struggle, including abrasions on his chest and knees. He also had hemorrhages on his neck. The deputy medical examiner, Dr. Adam Gonzalez. determined the cause of death was asphyxia due to neck and torso compression. The report said witnesses saw Lunas Campos "become unresponsive while being physically restrained by law enforcement." It did not elaborate on what happened during the struggle but cited evidence of injuries to his neck, head and torso associated with physical restraint. The report also noted the presence of petechial hemorrhages -- tiny blood spots from burst capillaries that can be associated with intense strain or injury -- in the eyelids and skin of the neck. Dr. Victor Weedn , a forensic pathologist who reviewed the autopsy report for AP, said the presence of petechiae in the eyes support the conclusion that asphyxia caused the death. Those injuries suggest pressure on the body and are often associated with such deaths, he said. He said the contusions on Lunas Campos' body may reflect physical restraint and the neck injuries were consistent with a hand or knee on the neck. The autopsy also found the presence of prescription antidepressant and antihistamine medications, adding that Lunas Campos had a history of bipolar disorder and anxiety. It made no mention of him attempting suicide. () STATE GOVERNMENT " ERCOT: Texas power grid is ready ahead of incoming winter storm" via - Texas grid officials say the state is prepared to meet electricity demand ahead of a powerful winter storm that's expected to bring days of freezing temperatures and the chance of ice or snow across parts of the state later this week. The Electric Reliability Council of Texas, which oversees the state's power grid, told The Texas Newsroom on Tuesday that based on expected weather conditions, it "anticipates there will be sufficient generation to meet demand" ahead of the storm. "ERCOT will continue to deploy all available resources to manage the grid reliably and coordinate closely with the Public Utility Commission, generation providers, and transmission utilities," the council said in a statement. Subfreezing temperatures are forecast to arrive by Friday as arctic air pushes south into Texas. Forecasters say moisture arriving late Friday night into Saturday could set the stage for hazardous winter weather throughout the state. (TPR) LOCAL GOVERNMENT " Grapevine-Colleyville ISD High School Receives Backlash for Hosting CAIR-Sponsored 'Islamic Games'" Meridith Dyer - Colleyville Heritage High School, part of Grapevine-Colleyville Independent School District (ISD), is scheduled to host the Dallas Islamic Games on May 9 and 10, 2026. According to the Islamic Games website, the event is North America's largest Muslim sports and athletic event and is "dedicated to promoting physical excellence, unity, and community development." () " Bexar County now allows contracts up to $100K to go without court approval" Andrea Drusch - Bexar County Commissioners Court is embracing a new policy that gives county department heads authority to make purchases up to $100,000 without coming before the elected leaders for approval. The change was made possible during the last Texas legislative session, and the five-member Commissioners Court largely agreed Tuesday they should make the change -- given the amount of frustration they've heard surrounding slow-moving contracts. "Hopefully what we'll see in return is a more effective and efficient process of executing contracts and the procurement process, which has always been a prior criticism," Bexar County Judge Peter Sakai said of the new policy. " ... We can move very fast as county government. We don't have to have that, 'Well, the county takes [forever].'" Earlier that morning, a voter registration vendor seeking to work with the county came before the court to air grievances about the process. () 2026 " Gov. Abbott endorses Nate Sheets over Sid Miller for agriculture commissioner," McGee \-- In a stunning blow to Texas Agriculture Commissioner Sid Miller , Gov. Greg Abbott endorsed Miller's Republican primary challenger for agriculture commissioner, putting his support behind first-time political candidate Nate Sheets. "Texans deserve an Agriculture Commissioner who is focused on promoting Texas Agriculture, with zero tolerance for criminality," Abbott wrote Wednesday on social media. "Nate Sheets is the true conservative champion for the job and is the leader we need to keep Texas the global powerhouse in agriculture." Last year, Miller turned heads when he hired his political consultant Todd Smith as the agency's chief of staff just a few months after after he was criminally charged for selling hemp licenses that are regulated by Miller's office. The move sparked outrage among agency employees they had warned Miller about Smith. Miller did not immediately respond to a request for comment. In a statement, Sheets said: "I'm honored to have Governor Abbott's support and I look forward to working together to fight for Texas agriculture and for farmers' and ranchers' future economic success, restore trust in our food system, and ensure Texas remains strong, healthy, and secure for generations to come." Sheets is the founder of Nature Nate's Honey company. A native Texan business and ranch owner, he served for six years in the U.S. Naval Reserve before graduating from Texas State University. Sheets sold Nature Nate's in 2021 and resigned as CEO in 2024 to run for agriculture commissioner. He also previously worked as communications director for E3 Partners, an evangelist ministry that establishes new Christian congregations around the world. In a statement, Kim Snyder , Abbott's campaign manager, said Abbott endorsed Sheets because of Miller's "history of corruption" and pointed to when Miller served in the Texas House. At the time, the measure had broad bipartisan support, but as the Republican Party has shifted further to the right, it has become a political sticking point among hardline anti-immigrant politicians. "Nate Sheets is the only candidate in the race who has the integrity to lead the Texas Department of Agriculture," Snyder added. () " Rep. James Talarico takes lead in Democratic Texas Senate primary poll" via - New polling shows state Rep. James Talarico leading the Democratic 2026 primary race for a Texas U.S. Senate seat. A new poll from Emerson College Polling and Nexstar Media shows Talarico, D-Austin, earning support from 47% of possible primary voters compared to 38% for U.S. Rep. Jasmine Crockett , D-Dallas, and 15% still undecided. "Talarico has built momentum among Hispanic (59%) and white (57%) voters, while a majority of Black Democratic primary voters (80%) support Crockett," Spencer Kimball , executive director of Emerson College Polling, noted in a news release. "Men also break for Talarico 52% to 30%, while women are about evenly split between the two Democrats, 44% for Talarico and 43% for Crockett." A head-to-head matchup between either of the leading Republican primary Senate candidates -- incumbent U.S. Sen. John Cornyn and Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton -- shows Talarico and Crockett fairing about the same. () " Beto O'Rourke won't endorse in Texas Senate Democratic primary" via - Beto O 'Rourke says he will not make an endorsement in the Democratic primary for Senate, calling U.S. Rep. Jasmine Crockett and state Rep. James Talarico "generational talents" who have what it takes to win. "I believe in the Democratic voters of the state of Texas, who are going to have a real close and personal look at these two phenomenal candidates," armed with appealing messages, fundraising skills and media presence, O'Rourke told Hearst Newspapers. Crockett and Talarico square off in the March 3 primary. Instead of picking a side, O'Rourke said he will focus on his Powered By People political action committee. He said that's aimed especially at young voters and relies on more personal engagement to boost turnout for the eventual nominee. "We're going to make sure we have enough net new Democratic voters who aren't just on the rolls, but are engaged, involved, informed and turn out to vote," O'Rourke said. () " A former MLB star is a frontrunner for TX-21. Critics say he's buying a seat." Bayliss Wagner - He's never held elected office and only once voted in a Republican primary. For most of his adult life, he lived far from Texas, building a standout baseball career. Mark "Tex" Teixeira might not fit the mold of a traditional candidate, but he has quickly emerged as a frontrunner in the race to succeed U.S. Rep. Chip Roy, R-Austin, in Congress. Teixeira is dominating the Republican primary for Texas' 21st Congressional District in cash on hand, loaning roughly $2 million to his own campaign and raising another $500,000 -- far beyond the funds reported so far by his opponents. He also has high-profile endorsements from Gov. Greg Abbott and 11 sitting members of Congress, among them House Majority WhipSteve Scalise and nine Texans. Teixeira has sought to portray himself as an analog to President Donald Trump -- a political outsider who's focused on tightening immigration rules, cutting "waste, fraud and abuse" and keeping "biological men out of our girls' sports." "I've been on a lot of great teams, and President Trump's team is one I want to be on to secure the border and crush the cartels," he said in a TV ad.
