| | For Immediate Release | CC'd The White House, White House Deputy Chief of Staff for Policy. January 22, 2026 – Grand Rapids, Michigan OP-ED: What If We Sterilize the Somali or Illegal Aliens, Girls 12–14 Yrs Old and Over Half the Women to Save Welfare Costs? What if we embark on a secret executive presidential order to sterilize more than half the Somali or illegal alien population in the US, rather than continue to pay for the fraud or increased burden of welfare? Girls as young as 12–14 years old and more than half the fertile female population are implanted with IUDs and other birth control methods, without their knowledge or consent and in some cases forced, to save rising welfare costs.
Undoubtedly, this would be a crime, and the perpetrators would swiftly be brought to justice, and rightly so. But this isn't what happened when this crime was recently discovered in Greenland. And we are not talking century-old occurrences but as recent as the 1990s and 2000s. The victims are still alive and so are the perpetrators that presided over these human rights crimes. Yet, not a single person has been held accountable.
This is what Denmark did to the people of Greenland. Except, the people of Greenland were not committing fraud, neither were they illegally invading Denmark; in fact, the opposite is true.In the 1990s and 2000s (and reports of cases continuing beyond into the 2000s), Danish authorities continued to implement a government-directed program in Greenland, known as the "Spiral Case," where approximately 4,500 Greenlandic women and girls, roughly half of the fertile female population at the time, had intrauterine devices (IUDs) inserted without their informed consent or knowledge. The program that initially began in the 1960s saw many as young as 12 or 13 coiled, and was designed to control population growth amid Danish concerns over rising birth rates amongst the people of Greenland and welfare costs. The insertions often caused severe pain, infections, infertility, and long-term trauma, and have been described by some Greenlandic leaders as a form of genocide or cultural erasure.
Some of the victims who are still alive today include Naja Lyberth (one of the first to speak publicly in 2017; she was 13–14 when fitted with an IUD), Jytte Lyberth (at age 14), Anne Lise Albrectsen (as a teenager), and others.
The perpetrators of these crimes are still alive in Denmark today. None have been prosecuted, let alone gone to prison for these crimes. Under intense pressure and with the looming U.S. takeover of Greenland, Denmark hastily offered a symbolic apology just a year or two ago for their many atrocities in Greenland, but not one person has been held accountable for this crime against the girls and women of Greenland.
Now, at the President's direction, we will continue negotiating with Denmark, and hope not to result in the use of force in Greenland. However, I'm asking the Vice President, the Secretary of State, and our Special Envoy to ask how the following persons who presided over these atrocities have never answered for these crimes.
The President is doing Denmark a huge favor by taking the approach of peaceful talks and talking to them as if they have any legitimate right to ownership of Greenland. The people of Greenland (Kalaallit, who form the vast majority of residents) never held a single vote or referendum to join or become part of Denmark.
Denmark is not a peaceful country living happily and singing kumbaya sing-alongs with the people of Greenland. It is a brutal colonial occupier that has no place in North America. Denmark has committed several human rights atrocities against the Inuit population of Greenland, from barbaric child experiments on Greenland's Inuit tribes to the forced sterilization of more than half the fertile female population without their consent mentioned above.
To be clear, I am in no way, shape, or form calling for this. I am merely using the hypothetical perspective of what the reaction would be if a similar crime were perpetrated against economic migrants or many illegal aliens in the United States, and remarking upon the paradox of Denmark portraying itself as a victim of injustice in the face of a potential U.S. takeover of Greenland, while simultaneously refusing to hold the perpetrators of these very real human rights crimes accountable. I am optimistic that the chance the President has given for peaceful negotiations and the eventual transfer of all of Greenland to the United States will be achieved, sooner rather than later; however, these are questions that still need to be answered by the Danish negotiators.

disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY TREY TRAINOR FOR TEXAS
body:
I defended Trump against Bragg's witch hunt – here's exactly what I said under oath

| | | | | | | [View this email in your browser](https://us10.campaign-archive.com/?e=4d3fe76c62&u=c9a64ea8a402e6526a97d9207&id=59edcb7d60)
---
[|
---](https://Trey4TX.us10.list-manage.com/track/click?u=c9a64ea8a402e6526a97d9207&id=50bd0018e2&e=4d3fe76c62)
| | | | | | Peter,

You may have seen my **June 2024 testimony** before the U.S. House Committee on the Judiciary, where I exposed the dangerous jurisdictional overreach by Manhattan DA **Alvin Bragg** in his case against **President Trump**. In fact, I’m the only candidate in this race who has worked directly with President Trump since 2016 and fought for President Trump through the entire Biden Presidency.
---
| | | | | | | | | | [|
---](https://Trey4TX.us10.list-manage.com/track/click?u=c9a64ea8a402e6526a97d9207&id=8bac896f85&e=4d3fe76c62)
| | |
As a former Commissioner and Chair of the Federal Election Commission (FEC), I made it clear that **only the FEC and Department of Justice** have authority over federal election laws – **not state or local officials** like Bragg weaponizing the law to target political opponents. This kind of abuse threatens the integrity of our elections and chills free speech. I testified that such actions set a perilous precedent and undermine consistent enforcement of our laws nationwide.
---
| |
As a lifelong conservative from right here in Texas, I've spent my career fighting for election integrity, defending our freedoms, and standing up against government overreach. Now, I'm asking for your support to take that same fight to Congress for Texas's 21st District.
---
| | | | | | | | | | | |
This wasn't my first time speaking truth to power in Washington. In September 2023, I testified before the House Committee on House Administration in the first formal oversight hearing of the FEC in over a decade. I warned against efforts to weaponize the FEC through partisan enforcement, which could silence conservative voices and undermine voter confidence. I called for reforms to prioritize consistent, impartial application of campaign finance laws – exactly what we need to prevent the kind of lawfare we saw under the Biden-Harris Administration.

body:
Knocking out this leg of the Voting Rights Act -- by weakening Section 2 -- would almost certainly reconstitute state legislatures, city councils, judicial districts, and every other type of political boundary in which racial minorities could be cut off from having a voice in their government.
This kind of change would silence untold numbers of voters and spiral our fight for voting rights back sixty years. RUSH $35 or more right now to help protect what the VRA stands for and defend our fundamental right to vote >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=012226_2&amount=35]
Voter Action Project [https://voteractionproject.org/]
Mother Jones: Republican Justices Appear Poised to Destroy What’s Left of the Voting Rights Act [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=012226_2&amount=25]
We'll hand this straight to Mother Jones, Team: " The Supreme Court, with its six-to-three Republican-appointed majority, appears ready to kneecap what remains of the Voting Rights Act’s protections for minority political representation. "
The descriptive language seems harsh, but the objective of these justices seems clear -- a complete dismantling of our seminal civil rights law . We've said it before and will say it again, but it's been clear long before the MAGA movement that Chief Justice Roberts has seen the removal of the VRA as one of his top goals for his time on the Court. It appears he may be on the cusp of succeeding.
During this week’s oral argument in Louisiana v. Callais , at least five conservative justices seemed ready to handicap the VRA so that it will no longer stop white majorities from locking racial minorities out of elected office through racial gerrymandering.
The consequences are simple to understand and grave for voter participation. The harder we make it to vote, the more politicians make voter participation feel worthless, the less people actually take part. Needless to say, the less people who participate, the less our democracy and our government looks like the people it's supposed to represent.
Team: We have to spread the word about this case and the consequences of dismantling the Voting Rights Act. Fuel our work with $35 or whatever you can today and help us defend the right to vote >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=012226_2&amount=35]
GIVE $15 NOW ➜ [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?express_lane=true&refcode=012226_2&amount=15] GIVE $25 NOW ➜ [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?express_lane=true&refcode=012226_2&amount=25]

GIVE $250 NOW ➜ [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?express_lane=true&refcode=012226_2&amount=250] Other Amount [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=012226_2&amount=35]
At issue in the case is Section 2 of the VRA, which requires that racial minorities have an equal opportunity to meaningfully participate in the electoral process. This provision has been used to strike down districting schemes and maps that prevented Black voters and other racial minorities from electing their preferred representatives. Since 1965, Section 2 has given people of color a seat at the table, from school boards to the halls of Congress. It appears this 60-year era is coming to an end.
“ Race is a part of redistricting always ,” Justice Sonia Sotomayor said, addressing the solicitor general from Louisiana, who was arguing against an existing map that had enabled the election of two Black members of Congress in his state. “ What you’re saying to us [is]...‘You can use [race] to help yourself achieve goals that reduce particular groups’ electoral participation, but you can’t use it to remedy that situation .’”
Striking down the last remnants of the Voting Rights Act is exactly why the Supreme Court held this case over from last year. Gutting Section 2 would take us backwards in time and allow racial gerrymandering to be a standard practice, silencing more voters. Just like the redistricting fights across the country, this is all about whether the party in power can choose their voters in order to stay in power in perpetuity.
We simply can't afford to go backwards like this. Will you chip in with $35 or more to help us fight back against these partisan efforts to silence voters? >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=012226_2&amount=35]

Integrity First Voter Action Project is dedicated to expanding ballot access and increasing voter participation across the country.
Since the Supreme Court gutted key provisions in the Voting Rights Act, extreme politicians have taken advantage to pass harsh laws that restrict access to the ballot box. These restrictions particularly affect disadvantaged communities and people of color. It’s our goal to bring awareness to these laws wherever they may crop up and organize voters to take action to ensure the right to vote is available to everyone in their states and communities.

The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. **Peter — Addressing sky high costs of living isn’t just a talking point for me, it is an urgent priority.**

I know people are struggling, making hard decisions to keep a roof over their heads, food on the table, the heat on, and winter clothes for their kids.

That’s why I’m fighting in Washington every day for Rhode Islanders. I won’t stop calling out politicians who are in Congress for selfish gain, who aren’t actively working to build a more affordable future for Americans. **I’m committed to the long fight so that future generations can realize the American Dream.**

| | Charlie would have wanted you to have this.

Before his September 10th assassination, Charlie had just put the finishing touches on a very important book. His final book.

The topic is one that Charlie found to be crucial for every human to understand and practice.

This isn't a book about public policy or political discourse, nor is it simply about passing on values of patriotism to young Americans.

**Instead, this book is about something far deeper and more personal -- the importance of honoring the Sabbath and resting in God's grace. **

Despite his hectic schedule and full life, Charlie was committed to setting aside an entire day each week to rest, to pray, and to give undivided attention to God, Erika, and his children.

By honoring the Sabbath, Charlie lived out a powerful message: _**" God, You are enough. And because You are enough, I need not carry the weight of a world that was never mine to hold." **_

His book, _**Stop, in the Name of God**_ is the fruit of that conviction.

When you read it, you will hear Charlie's voice inviting you to reclaim something our fast-paced culture has essentially erased: a time for rest, a time devoted to God, and time with family.

Charlie's hope was for each of us to rediscover the Sabbath as he did: not as a burden to bear, but as a gift to receive...

A sacred routine meant to draw us nearer to God, to steady our hearts with His peace, and renew our strength for the battles to which He calls us.

I believe you will find this book inspiring.

Charlie wanted everyone to have this book because its message meant so much in his own life.

In the months since Charlie's assassination, there has been a massive surge of interest in Turning Point USA's message among young Americans...

...and it's not just the conservative message as a whole -- _**it 's the message of FAITH! **_

In recent months, I have heard countless stories of people who have answered Charlie's call to attend a Bible study, start a family, and pray to God.

Charlie devoted so much of his time urging people to build strong families, to go to church, and to stand up for America. _And it 's happening. _

After years of witnessing declining church attendance, we are now seeing Americans filling the pews in huge numbers across the country.

What we're witnessing is not just growth --**it 's revival. **

At Turning Point USA, we are dedicated and honored to continue strengthening the faith of Americans, young and old.

We are building a coalition of truth-preaching churches that stand firm against cultural compromise, defend biblical values, and strengthen families.

We are training pastors, uniting congregations, and, of course, reaching the next generation on campuses across the country with this same message.

You might feel disheartened by the evil in our culture and by the unthinkable assassination of Charlie.

**But America 's faithful are waking up. The youth are waking up. America is waking up. **

All across this nation, pastors are linking arms, young believers are finding their voice, and families are saying, _" We're not backing down." _

This is what Charlie prayed for.

I see this book as one of Charlie's most enduring gifts to the world, and I know you will too.

None of us knew how brief his time on earth would be. But the truths written in this book are timeless. They will outlive us all, and most importantly, **_so will the legacy of Charlie 's faith. _**

Charlie lived life at a relentless pace, but he also understood the sacred value of stillness. Through it all, his gaze was fixed on eternity with God.

My name is **Corporal Frank S. Wright** , United States Marine Corps, retired. I'm a hundred years old now -- one of the last living Marine Raiders of World War II.In January 1942, just weeks after the attack on Pearl Harbor, I quit high school in Arkansas and walked into the enlistment office. I was sixteen -- too young, too skinny, and too light to qualify. The sergeant told me to come back when I was heavier.So I went home, ate all the bananas I could find, and stuffed five pounds' worth into my pockets before stepping on that scale again.I passed. I lied about my age. And I became a Marine.

After boot camp, I volunteered to join the **4th Marine Raiders** , America's first special operations unit.They asked me why I wanted to join. I said, _" Because I want to fight."_Our commanding officer was **James Roosevelt** , the President's son -- a good man, the kind who never gave an order he wouldn't do himself. We were trained to land first, fight behind enemy lines, and take the beaches nobody else could reach.From **Guadalcanal** to **New Georgia** , from the jungles of the Solomons to the black sand of **Iwo Jima** , we fought to free the Pacific.On **Guam** , I was stabbed in the stomach during hand-to-hand combat. On **Iwo Jima** , I was hit by machine-gun fire and knocked unconscious. Both times, my men thought I was gone. Somehow, I wasn't.When I came to, I saw the flag rising on Mount Suribachi. Every ship in the harbor sounded its horn. I had tears in my eyes then, and I still do when I think about it.That flag meant freedom still lived.

I'll now admit, I was always a little rebellious. When the war ended, I became a drill instructor, helping shape the next generation of Marines. I was in my twenties, carrying wounds inside and out.For more than a decade, I didn't share my stories. I kept them locked away, like many of my brothers did. Not just my story, but those of the men who never came home, and those who are no longer here to tell theirs. They've given old Marines like me a place to share what we lived through, to look young cadets and future service members in the eye and say, "This is what it means to serve."They've brought veterans from every generation together -- to remember, to teach, and to inspire. And every year, the American Veterans Center Annual Conference gives us something rare -- a gathering where history stands shoulder to shoulder with the future.It's where I've met cadets who listen with the same wide eyes I once had at sixteen. It's where old comrades find each other again, and where we all remember that the values we fought for -- courage, duty, honor -- are still being carried forward.It's a living bridge between those who fought for freedom and those who will defend it next. The National Memorial Day Parade in Washington, D.C., where America gathers to honor its heroes. The Annual Veterans Conference each November, where we share stories and pass the torch to those who will serve next. The preservation of our stories through documentaries and oral histories -- so that when we are gone, the lessons remain. At my age, I don't take many things for granted. But I still believe in this country -- in what it stands for, and in the people who keep its history alive.If you believe that too, I ask you to help the American Veterans Center continue its work. So that long after the last of us is gone, our voices will still be heard -- reminders of what America can be when its people stand together.Thank you for remembering. Thank you for caring. And thank you for keeping faith with those who served.Semper Fidelis, Frank S. Wright Corporal, U.S. Marine Corps (Ret.) Veteran, 4th Marine Raiders | 21st Marines, 3rd Marine Division P.S.** When I was sixteen, I had to lie about my age to fight for my country. Now, at one hundred, I can tell you the truth as plain as I know it: freedom isn't free, and the stories of those who fought for it are fading fast. Your gift -- whatever you can give -- helps make sure they're never forgotten. The mission of the American Veterans Center and the World War II Veterans Committee is to preserve and promote the legacy and experiences of America's veterans and active duty service personnel from World War II through today. A non-profit educational organization, the AVC and WWIIVC are funded solely through generous contributions from people like you. All contributions are tax-deductible. Peter,
When I was in Congress, I once took to the House floor to discuss something that might sound mundane to some people: dishwashers.
**As a single mom, I know _a lot_ about dishwashers.** I load and unload mine over and over. I saved and skimped and was so proud when I got a new dishwasher—just like so many other Californians.
At the time, Congress wanted to pass a bill about dishwashers. One of my Republican colleagues claimed to be an expert on them, but [couldn’t answer](https://act.katieporter.com/go/21698?t=3&akid=40736%2E3422442%2EVdr9J-) basic questions about how they work or how much they cost.
Despite that, Republicans wanted to have their way on the legislation.
Here’s the thing: if you want to write the rules we all have to live by—from dishwashers to the cost of living—you should probably understand what everyday life actually looks like for the people you represent.
**Many of my opponents in this race for governor don’t.** One is a billionaire that needs a team of consultants to explain what life’s like for folks struggling to get by. Others only care about corporate interests, and don’t pay attention to the needs of working Californians.
I know how to handle guys like this because I spent years doing it for my constituents in Washington. As governor, I’ll bring that same energy to Sacramento and make sure we hold people who have no idea what it’s like to struggle accountable.

This episode of **AMPED UP** was equal parts political strategy session, media critique, and brutally honest diagnosis of the moment America is living through. [Cliff Schecter](https://open.substack.com/users/31941177-cliff-schecter?utm_source=mentions) and [David Shuster](https://open.substack.com/users/16891317-david-shuster?utm_source=mentions) were joined by veteran Democratic strategist [Mike Nellis](https://open.substack.com/users/313054292-mike-nellis?utm_source=mentions) for a wide-ranging, unsparing conversation about Donald Trump's visible mental and physical decline, Democratic messaging failures, the Epstein files, billionaire capture of government, and what a winning 2026-2028 strategy actually looks like.

Funny, furious, and razor-sharp, the episode kept returning to one core question: why does the Democratic Party keep underselling the chaos, corruption, and cruelty right in front of everyone?
* * *
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuYmx1ZWFtcC5jby9zdWJzY3JpYmU_.5R4KssA9aeUWz83HjugIH8ljr19A2rxbPAOSgLp69Dw?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=185442876)
* * *
### **1\. Trump 's Cognitive Decline Is No Longer Subtle**
* The panel breaks down Trump's bizarre letter to Norway, his confusion over Greenland vs. Iceland, and increasingly erratic public behavior.
* Shuster and Nellis argue the evidence of decline is obvious--but Democrats still hesitate to say it plainly.
* The group stresses this isn't "gaffes," it's judgment failure with global consequences.

### **2\. Why Democrats Won 't Weaponize Trump's Weakness**
* Republicans relentlessly branded Biden as old and infirm--successfully.
* Democrats, by contrast, refuse to apply the same framing to Trump.
* Nellis argues Democrats are right to focus on the economy, but wrong to ignore how Trump's instability directly harms it.

### **3\. The Economy, Corruption, and Security: One Story, Not Three**
* Nellis lays out his core messaging framework: economy, safety, corruption.
* Trump's tariffs, trade threats, and foreign policy blunders all reinforce a single narrative--weak leadership serving billionaires.
* The hosts argue Democrats must stop siloing issues and start telling a unified story.
* * *
[Share](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=3722532&post_id=185442876&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_content=share&utm_campaign=email-share&action=share&triggerShare=true&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MTg1NDQyODc2LCJpYXQiOjE3NjkxMjEzOTksImV4cCI6MTc3MTcxMzM5OSwiaXNzIjoicHViLTM3MjI1MzIiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.iLQpQp6zGSOyCeyaHp35FID3KLXH-7lBwVJhyfDxkkY)
* * *

### **4\. Epstein: The Gateway Issue Democrats Are Afraid to Use**
* The panel tears into the administration's refusal to release Epstein files despite legal requirements.
* Epstein is framed as the perfect connective tissue: elite corruption, abuse of power, billionaire impunity.
* Nellis calls it the rare issue that depresses Trump's base, enrages independents, and unifies Democrats.

### **5\. Media Failure and the Normalization of Authoritarian Behavior**
* The group slams mainstream media for euphemisms and cowardice--"What is the DOJ hiding?" instead of "They're protecting Trump."
* Comparisons are drawn between past political "scandals" and today's normalization of abuse, secrecy, and violence.
* The conversation highlights how far the political Overton window has shifted.

### **6\. What a Winning Democratic Candidate Actually Looks Like**
* Governors--not senators--are seen as the strongest 2028 contenders.
* Purple-state executive experience, anti-corruption credibility, and economic populism are essential.
* Names discussed include Midwestern and Southern governors who can speak plainly and project strength without coastal elitism.

Peter,

Two big things have stayed with me for the last 53 years, since _Roe v. Wade_ was decided on this day in 1973.

First: The decision was momentous, an event to be celebrated, and _permanent_. In other words, when the U.S. Supreme Court issued its decision confirming a constitutional right to bodily autonomy, **it was unfathomable to think that the precedent set that day could be ignored or invalidated at _any_ point in the future.** If you had told me then that women in 2026 would have fewer rights than we had in 1973, I would have been shocked... _and very, very angry._

Second: _Roe_ was so important for _everyone_ of childbearing age — but the deepest reaction came from anyone who had gone through the process of getting an abortion pre-_Roe_. I’ve talked to women who had horrible experiences in dark and dirty hidden "medical" offices, who dealt with serious health problems caused by the procedure, who were terrified others would find out. The trauma of needing care in a country that outlawed it has stayed with them, which is why the women who still live with those memories are some of the most ardent warriors in today’s pro-choice movement. Those of us who were alive pre-Roe are DETERMINED that young women will not have to undergo similar, terrible experiences.

I am furious that we had more rights in 1973 than we have today. But I am also hopeful, because we have something that didn't exist yet in 1973: We have the millions-strong community of EMILYs List candidates and supporters. We have a movement.

clean_body: Roe v. Wade should be 53 years old today. | = I am furious that we had more rights in 1973 than we have today. But I am also hopeful, because we have something that didn't exist yet in 1973: We have the millions-strong community of EMILYs List candidates and supporters. We have a movement. = | = Peter, Two big things have stayed with me for the last 53 years, since Roe v. Wade was decided on this day in 1973. First: The decision was momentous, an event to be celebrated, and permanent. In other words, when the U.S. Supreme Court issued its decision confirming a constitutional right to bodily autonomy, it was unfathomable to think that the precedent set that day could be ignored or invalidated at any point in the future. If you had told me then that women in 2026 would have fewer rights than we had in 1973, I would have been shocked... and very, very angry. Second: Roe was so important for everyone of childbearing age — but the deepest reaction came from anyone who had gone through the process of getting an abortion pre-Roe. I’ve talked to women who had horrible experiences in dark and dirty hidden "medical" offices, who dealt with serious health problems caused by the procedure, who were terrified others would find out. The trauma of needing care in a country that outlawed it has stayed with them, which is why the women who still live with those memories are some of the most ardent warriors in today’s pro-choice movement. Those of us who were alive pre-Roe are DETERMINED that young women will not have to undergo similar, terrible experiences. I am furious that we had more rights in 1973 than we have today. But I am also hopeful, because we have something that didn't exist yet in 1973: We have the millions-strong community of EMILYs List candidates and supporters. We have a movement. This is not a drill and it’s not a bad dream.
# [](https://act.betoorourke.com/go/43706?t=1&akid=240627%2E444211%2EtoKIwt)
[](https://act.betoorourke.com/go/56109?c0=pbp-em-20260122-split.uT61Ws&refcode=ema20260122-240627&t=3&akid=240627%2E444211%2EtoKIwt)
_Let me lay this out, clear as day:_
I am the only Democratic Senator up for reelection in a state Trump won in 2024.
This Senate race in Georgia will be the most competitive and most expensive in the nation.
If you’re outraged by what’s happening to our country — and you’re ready to fight — [**please split $5 between my reelection campaign and Powered by People today.**](https://act.betoorourke.com/go/56109?c0=pbp-em-20260122-split.uT61Ws&refcode=ema20260122-240627&t=4&akid=240627%2E444211%2EtoKIwt)
**[SPLIT A DONATION](https://act.betoorourke.com/go/56109?c0=pbp-em-20260122-split.uT61Ws&refcode=ema20260122-240627&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=5&akid=240627%2E444211%2EtoKIwt)**
Otherwise, let me remind you why I ran for Senate — and why this moment is just as urgent.
Before I was elected, I led investigations of corruption and human rights abuses worldwide. We exposed wrongdoing in countries where criticizing the government is dangerous, where whistleblowers and witnesses will only meet in secret, where protest carries the risk of prosecution.
More and more, the atmosphere under Trump reminded me of those places where dissent was silenced by intimidation.
Trump’s rise wasn’t just a crisis. It was a warning.
I ran for Senate because I saw the danger in electing someone so profoundly unfit for the presidency and I wanted to confront the corruption that made his rise possible.
I also ran — years before the _Dobbs_ decision — because it was already clear the GOP was coming for reproductive rights. I saw Georgia as the front line in that fight. With a six-week ban now in place here, and Republicans pushing for a national abortion ban, it still is.
**Now this President is staging a power grab unprecedented in our history:**
* He’s freed violent criminals who attacked the Capitol on his behalf.
* Purged independent watchdogs across government.
* Stacked key agencies with loyalists — and called on them to investigate his political opponents.
* Defied and threatened federal judges.
* Undermined the press.

Trump’s goal isn’t just revenge. He wants to use the government to crush the opposition. And now, Americans are living in fear of their own government.
This is not a drill and it’s not a bad dream. As citizens, it is the test of our lifetimes.
**In 2020, the pundits said flipping a Republican Senate seat in Georgia couldn’t be done. But we built one of the strongest voter mobilization programs in Senate campaign history — and we won. That victory won the Senate majority.**
Now we must win again. And we _will_ win again.
Just like last time, I can’t do it alone.
So I’m asking:
[**Please split a contribution between my reelection campaign and Powered by People today, of $5 or any amount that works for you.**](https://act.betoorourke.com/go/56109?c0=pbp-em-20260122-split.uT61Ws&refcode=ema20260122-240627&t=6&akid=240627%2E444211%2EtoKIwt)
The average online donation to our campaign is around $30. Many give less. Some give more.
All that matters is that lots and lots of people are contributing what they can to power our grassroots campaign. Please, contribute today.
**[Donate $3](https://act.betoorourke.com/go/56109?c0=pbp-em-20260122-split.uT61Ws&refcode=ema20260122-240627&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=25&akid=240627%2E444211%2EtoKIwt)**
Thanks for being part of this team.
As always,
Jon Ossoff

| Friend, This is Cisco Aguilar, Nevada’s Secretary of State. Hi Peter, Some great news to share: **I’m proud to have earned the endorsement of the National Nurses Union -- the largest organization of registered nurses in the country!** [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/123844666/596754848/949478007?refcode=em-1.22.26-all-b&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjIvMS8xMTc1MjUiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiOGIxYjY3NzQtZTZmNy1mMDExLThkNGMtMDAyMjQ4MmQyNzliIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=K5OWLMp5IEF8Mw89T_MGNGlzayjd4HjTUKCc_n9DByo=) Nurses are the _backbone_ of our health care system who are on the front lines every day -- standing up when the system puts profits ahead of people. They’re the most trusted profession in America because they fight for their patients and are unafraid to tell the truth. That’s why this endorsement means so much to me. The National Nurses Union knows what’s at stake in this race. They see firsthand what happens when politicians slash Medicaid, undermine the Affordable Care Act, and put corporate interests ahead of patients. name: Deb Haaland
subject: Did you know that I used to work at a local bakery?
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR AND AUTHORIZED BY DEB FOR NEW MEXICO**
body:
Working so many different jobs is how I learned what it really takes to get by.

| | | [](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/134?t=1&akid=7014%2E400544%2EQIzGoY)
---
[](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/4206?refcode=jtk167-fr-nd&t=2&akid=7014%2E400544%2EQIzGoY)
Did you know that, before I became an organizer and got into public service, I worked at a local bakery in Southeast Albuquerque, friend?
As the daughter of a Pueblo woman who grew up in a military family, I was taught the value of hard work from a young age. Moving often meant learning to adapt quickly and do whatever work was in front of me.

Over the years, I’ve worked a lot of different jobs. I started at my local bakery right after high school, held jobs in catering, worked at my child’s preschool, and even started my own small business producing and canning homemade salsa.

I know what it’s like to work hard just to get by. Those experiences shaped me, and it’s why I fight for working families.
_If you've saved payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately:_ | | | [Donate $10 >>](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/4405?refcode=jtk167-fr-nd&t=3&akid=7014%2E400544%2EQIzGoY)

---

---
New Mexicans know what it’s like to work multiple jobs just to put food on the table, to make ends meet. I know that struggle too. Every day, as hard as it was, I got up and kept going.
**
I was determined to build a brighter future for myself and my family, but I was up against a system — and leaders — who weren’t fighting for me. Leaders should understand what people are going through and work to make life easier, not harder. That’s the kind of leader I am.**
**Working so many different jobs is how I learned what it really takes to get by.** Those experiences made me the fierce, hardworking person, mother, and leader I am today.
**It’s why I know families here in New Mexico need a raise — so let’s increase the minimum wage and expand the child tax credit. It’s why we should stop medical debt from showing up on credit reports. It’s why we should give kids real career pathways starting in middle school and through high school, with hands-on experience. It’s why we should expand the opportunity scholarship for kids who know they want to go to college. And it’s why we need to lower bills, ensure cheaper rent, and build a stronger economy that actually works for working families.

_But I can’t make that happen without you._**
**_[Please, can I count on you to chip in $5, or whatever you can comfortably spare, now to help me become governor of New Mexico and build a future where everyone can thrive?](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/4404?refcode=jtk167-fr-nd&t=7&akid=7014%2E400544%2EQIzGoY)_**

Deb

clean_body: Working so many different jobs is how I learned what it really takes to get by. | | | Did you know that, before I became an organizer and got into public service, I worked at a local bakery in Southeast Albuquerque, friend? As the daughter of a Pueblo woman who grew up in a military family, I was taught the value of hard work from a young age. Moving often meant learning to adapt quickly and do whatever work was in front of me. Over the years, I’ve worked a lot of different jobs. I started at my local bakery right after high school, held jobs in catering, worked at my child’s preschool, and even started my own small business producing and canning homemade salsa. I know what it’s like to work hard just to get by. Those experiences shaped me, and it’s why I fight for working families. If you've saved payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately: | | | | | | | | | New Mexicans know what it’s like to work multiple jobs just to put food on the table, to make ends meet. I know that struggle too. Every day, as hard as it was, I got up and kept going. I was determined to build a brighter future for myself and my family, but I was up against a system — and leaders — who weren’t fighting for me. Leaders should understand what people are going through and work to make life easier, not harder. That’s the kind of leader I am. Working so many different jobs is how I learned what it really takes to get by. Those experiences made me the fierce, hardworking person, mother, and leader I am today. It’s why I know families here in New Mexico need a raise — so let’s increase the minimum wage and expand the child tax credit. It’s why we should stop medical debt from showing up on credit reports. name: David Hogg
subject: This is not going to end well
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY LEADERS WE DESERVE, LEADERSWEDESERVE
body:
Not a single county in six states has reached herd immunity for kindergartners.
# [](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/852?refcode=em20260122-1&t=1&akid=3076%2E587540%2Ec_xyrv)
I'll be blunt, Peter: This absolutely _will not turn out well._
Not a single county in Idaho, Louisiana, Oregon, Tennessee, Utah, or Wisconsin has reached kindergarten herd immunity thresholds for vaccinations. **Not one.**
This country eradicated measles in 2000. Declared polio eliminated in 1994. Now, we are watching vaccination rates plummet due to misinformation, conspiracy theories, and politicians who refuse to stand up for basic facts of public health.
Kids are going to get sick. Some _will die._
This is not a hypothetical. It's a preventable reality caused by **diseases we've already beaten.**
The opposition has played a 50-year game to get here, promoting media that spreads lies, appointing judges and officials who gut public health programs, people who treat science like it's optional. It's our children who will pay the price.
But here's what I know:
**There are young, educated, and fearless leaders across the country ready to fight back.** Ready to stand up to extremism, protect our communities, and put kids' health over bullshit culture wars. And Leaders We Deserve is ready to help them get elected and make lasting change.
Thank you,
David Hogg

Just recently, I learned that former Fox News host Jeanine Pirro, U.S. Attorney for the District of Columbia, asked to interview me.

This is on top of the FBI’s Counterterrorism Division’s inquiry at the end of last year.

**As a former CIA officer, I've seen democracies flicker out. I’ve seen what life is like when a government is rigged. I’ve studied this kind of political authoritarianism in other countries where you can't criticize the guys in charge without getting a knock at the door in the middle of the night.**

It’s hard to believe I am talking about it in my own country, and the knock is happening on my door.

I've always tried to be straight with you in these emails. When these threats happen, it requires a strategy -- because no American wants to live in a country where the president can weaponize the government against his perceived enemies.

name: Chris Brooks, LCV
subject: New EPA policy: Lives saved don’t count when setting air pollution rules
body:
This is a dangerous new low. We need to hear from you.

If you are unable to see the message below, [click here to view](https://links.messages.lcv.org/servlet/MailView?ms=MTM0MjI1NjIS1&r=NjA3MDU0MTAzNTc3S0&j=MjM4MDI0MjI0NgS2&mt=1&rt=0).
| | | |
---
|
* * *
---
| | | | DEVELOPING...Trump’s EPA is discarding how clean air rules have been made for decades, making it federal policy to _ignore_ the value of human lives and health.
---
| | **This is one of the most reckless and outright dangerous moves we’ve seen yet from the Trump administration.**
---
| | With this new announcement, we need to mobilize in a serious way. That means ramping up organizing on the ground around the country — and ensuring Trump and his Republican backers in Congress pay a real political price for the damage he's causing. **Because this moment is so important, a group of donors has agreed to 3X MATCH all contributions.**
---
| | [**_Our 2026 Membership Drive is underway, and the most important thing you can do right now is renew your LCV membership for just $5 to oppose these efforts to rewrite the rules that put polluter profits before people._**](https://links.messages.lcv.org/els/v2/w_)
---
| | _**_WHAT’S HAPPENING_**_
---
| | For decades, the EPA has set pollution rules that factored in the health benefits of cleaner air for the public — including fewer asthma attacks, lower rates of heart and lung disease, fewer hospital visits, and fewer premature deaths. Decades of pollution standards have saved tens of billions of dollars and hundreds of thousands of lives.
---
| | **Now, under Trump, the EPA plans to stop counting those health benefits in its decision-making; the cost of a human life is now $0, the cost of an ER visit triggered by air pollution is — you guessed it — $0.**
---
| | Instead, the EPA will calculate only the financial costs to _corporations_ of complying with pollution rules, while _stripping out_ the economic value of protecting public health. The shift would apply to rules covering some of **the most dangerous and widespread air pollutants in the country.**
---
| | Fine particle pollution and smog are linked to asthma, heart and lung disease, and premature death. Even moderate exposure can cause serious, lasting harm to our health, with children, seniors, communities near industrial sites, and low-income communities bearing the greatest risk. The Trump administration wants to keep the public IN THE DARK about how many more people will die, how many more kids will have asthma attacks, how many more ER visits for heart attacks and strokes will happen as it eliminates pollution standards for power plants, cars and trucks, and other industries.
---
| | **Bottom line: Whether they count it or not, Trump’s rollbacks mean dirtier air, worse health outcomes, sicker communities, and higher costs for us all.**
---
| |
## **League of Conservation Voters**
**2026 Membership Drive**
**FOR IMMEDIATE REVIEW**
**Supporter Record:** Peter Willis
**DONATED TO JANUARY MEMBERSHIP DRIVE?** NOT YET **Member Status:**[**_PENDING — Renew your membership now for just $5_**](https://links.messages.lcv.org/els/v2/YYbZBxgg_Xs~)
---
| | _**_HOW YOU CAN HELP_**_
---
| | Here’s the thing: Trump’s moves to undo basic safety protections are wildly unpopular, even in red states. He can only get away with this if we stay silent.
---
| | LCV is mobilizing people across the country to oppose dangerous attacks on clean air, applying grassroots pressure and working to hold politicians accountable when they side with polluters over the people they were elected to serve.
---
| | The strength of our response depends on the size and commitment of LCV members. The more people we reach, the bigger chance we have to undo some of Trump’s worst policies.
---
| | [**Right now, you can help by renewing your LCV membership while membership is just $5. Every dollar of your support will be TRIPLED to help us reach our $50,000 goal >>**](https://links.messages.lcv.org/els/v2/L6b_)
---
| | This action — and this moment — are dangerous. But it’s also one where collective action can make a real difference in our future. When we work together to speak out, organize, and demand better, we _can_ protect our communities.
---
| | With hope,
---
| | | | Chris Brooks
Vice President of Membership
League of Conservation Voters

| | FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE January 22, 2026
Doug Lloyd Makes Commanding Case for Attorney General in NORC Debate
Veteran Prosecutor's Experience Stands in Stark Contrast to Opponent
WATERFORD, MI -- Eaton County Prosecutor Doug Lloyd delivered a decisive and disciplined performance at the Michigan Attorney General debate hosted by the North Oakland Republican Club (NORC), clearly demonstrating why his 30 years as a career prosecutor uniquely qualify him to serve as Michigan's next Republican Attorney General.
The debate was moderated by former State Representative and Attorney General candidate Ryan Berman and former State Senate Floor Majority Leader Mike Kowall.
Throughout the evening, Lloyd distinguished himself by grounding his answers in real world experience prosecuting violent crime, enforcing the rule of law, and managing complex legal decisions that directly impact public safety. While opponent Kevin Kijewski spoke from the perspective of a divorce attorney, Lloyd articulated how decades inside the criminal justice system, not the civil courtroom, prepare a candidate to lead Michigan's top law enforcement office.
"This race is about electability and who is prepared to do the job on Day One." Lloyd said. "This race will be won by an experienced prosecutor and I am in this race to make sure it's a Republican."
Doug Lloyd currently serves as the elected Prosecutor of Eaton County and has more than 30 years of experience as a career prosecutor. He is endorsed by more than 60 county prosecutors, 30 sheriffs, and the Police Officers Association of Michigan, reflecting broad support from those who work on the front lines of public safety.

# Barron Trump APOLOGIZES to rude UK operator while saving friend's life
Barron Trump, calling from the US, **[alerted British police](https://substack.com/redirect/d64c0a38-436a-41b1-a1e8-7cf618fdc118?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** after witnessing a violent assault on a close female friend during a FaceTime call from London on January 18, 2025. When the 999 operator accused him of being rude for dodging personal details, the 19-year-old calmly apologized--"I'm so sorry for being rude"--and urged swift action, potentially saving her life as she later testified in court.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/d64c0a38-436a-41b1-a1e8-7cf618fdc118?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Operator Rebukes Caller:** The emergency handler demanded Barron stop being rude and answer questions precisely about his connection to the victim, frustrating the urgent call as he focused on the ongoing beating.
* **Victim Credits Heroic Intervention:** The assaulted woman told jurors at Snaresbrook Crown Court that Barron's timely 999 call was "a sign from God" and directly helped save her life amid the brutal attack.
* **Suspect Faces Serious Charges:** Russian national Matvei Rumiantsev, 22, stands accused of assault, strangling, rape, and obstruction after allegedly attacking the woman in a jealous rage at his east London flat.

# Tennis star shuts down reporter for baiting her to trash America
American tennis star Amanda Anisimova **[firmly rebuffed a reporter](https://substack.com/redirect/d978e07b-01b0-40dc-a853-564cadb2a603?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** at the Australian Open who probed her feelings about representing the U.S. flag amid recent domestic events, declaring she's "always proud" and dismissing the question as irrelevant.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/821406ae-58d4-4777-bbb9-b5433ce02055?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* **Proud American Identity**
Born in the U.S., Anisimova expressed unwavering pride in representing her country and praised the strong performances of American athletes across both tours at the tournament.
* **Post-Match Press Conference**
The exchange occurred after her commanding second-round victory (6-1, 6-4) over Czech player Katerina Siniakova, advancing her in the 2026 Australian Open draw.
* **Reporter 's Persistent Probing**
When pressed on whether recent U.S. developments complicated her feelings, Anisimova bluntly shut it down, stating the political angle was not relevant to her tennis focus.

# Mamdani defends Pro-Palestine activist claims deportation attempt was an attack
New York City Mayor **[Zohran Mamdani fiercely defended](https://substack.com/redirect/9e0441a9-6434-4220-8e01-435d8132d97e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** Syrian-born Columbia activist Mahmoud Khalil on Thursday, branding the Trump administration's push to deport him an assault on free speech and human rights advocacy.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/9e0441a9-6434-4220-8e01-435d8132d97e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Deportation Threat Escalates**
Trump officials accuse Khalil of green card fraud and Hamas ties, invoking a rare statute to deport him to Syria or Algeria after a recent appeals court ruling overturned his prior protections.
* **Khalil 's Activism Background**
The 31-year-old former Columbia grad student was arrested by ICE last year for his role in pro-Palestinian campus protests, spending months detained in Louisiana before temporary release.

At a Brooklyn press conference, the mayor declared Khalil a true New Yorker deserving to stay, vowing to advocate for him amid what he calls broader suppression of pro-human rights speech.Beijing--who said "People just make up so much nonsense about China."
